name: Ragen Davey
subject: Act Today: Speak out against a plan to fast-track oil and gas drilling in Alaska!
body:
Submit a public comment against recklessly speeding up fossil fuel developments in the NPR-A!

Submit a public comment against recklessly speeding up fossil fuel developments in the NPR-A!
                  

(https://support.defenders.org/s/5607698/38SyG9Xl)

(https://support.defenders.org/s/5607699/38SyG9Xl)

Defender,

The Bureau of Land Management is now deciding whether to fast-track oil and gas development in a massive stretch of wildlife habitat known as the National Petroleum Alaska-Reserve.

The Reserve is home to an incredible array of animals, including caribou, polar bears, migratory birds and more. These animals are currently protected by safeguards that BLM could decide to weaken, putting their lives and homes in danger.

The public comment process is open now: Click here to send your comment to BLM opposing weakening rules that protect wildlife in the Reserve! (https://support.defenders.org/s/5607700/38SyG9Xl)

This process was kicked off by a request from the Alaska Oil and Gas Association to create a new, fast-tracked permitting framework to build roads, pipelines, gravel pads, and other oilfield infrastructure.

Those sped-up permits would face less scrutiny with fewer opportunities for public review and input. If secured, there will be no opportunity for public engagement on any future proposed oil and gas activity in the Reserve, regardless of the size and scope of the project.

The Reserve could be industrialized with oil and gas development even faster than before – driving some animals out of their home turf and closer to the edge of extinction.

BLM is taking public comments until the July 6 deadline. We must speak up today before the public is cut out of decision-making processes in this important and rich landscape!

Keep polar bears and other Arctic animals safe: Tell BLM not to weaken vital protections that protect wildlife in the Reserve! (https://support.defenders.org/s/5607701/38SyG9Xl)

Defender, thank you for taking the time to speak up on behalf of wildlife in Alaska and beyond.

Thank you,

Ragen Davey

Representative, Alaska

Defenders of Wildlife

(http://www.facebook.com/DefendersofWildlife) (http://twitter.com/defenders) (https://www.instagram.com/defendersofwildlife/?hl=en) (http://www.youtube.com/defendersofwildlife) (https://www.tiktok.com/@defendersofwildlife)

Defenders of Wildlife 1130 17th Street NW • Washington, DC 20036 defenders.org (https://defenders.org)

Friend, I wanted to do something a little bit different today and share a piece I recently co-wrote alongside my colleague, _**Councilwoman Dr. Michalyn Easter-Thomas.**_ As we work together to move Memphis forward, we believe that taking care of the people who take care of our city is just common sense. Every day, City of Memphis employees show up to serve our community. They collect our trash, maintain our parks, respond to emergencies, keep our libraries running, process permits, support neighborhoods, and provide countless other services that make our city function. **When those employees welcome a new child into their family,__Memphis should show up for them.__** That is why we support establishing _**paid parental leave**_ for City of Memphis employees. **A Practical Investment, Not a Luxury** Paid parental leave is not a luxury. It is a practical investment in working families, our workforce, and the future of our city. No parent should have to choose between bonding with a newborn and paying their bills. Yet for many workers across the country, that remains the reality. According to the _Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)_ , the United States remains the only OECD member country without paid maternity leave at the national level. While some states have adopted their own paid leave programs, _millions of American workers still lack access to paid parental leave._ Recent research from the _Pew Research Center_ found that nearly seven in ten Americans support requiring employers to provide paid family leave, reflecting a growing recognition that supporting families and supporting a strong workforce go hand in hand. Support for paid leave extends across political parties, demonstrating that helping working families is a value shared by Americans from a variety of backgrounds and viewpoints. **Supporting Every Kind of Family** The earliest weeks and months of a child's life matter. Medical professionals and child development experts have long emphasized the importance of parent-child bonding during infancy. Those early interactions help lay the foundation for healthy emotional, cognitive, and physical development. And this conversation is _not just about mothers._ Fathers, adoptive parents, foster parents, and all caregivers deserve the opportunity to spend meaningful time with a new child. Strong families come in many forms, and our policies should recognize that reality. **Strengthening Our Workforce** Paid parental leave also makes sense from a workforce perspective. Cities across the nation are increasingly adopting family-friendly workplace policies because they understand a simple truth: retaining experienced employees is more cost-effective than constantly recruiting and training new ones. Research consistently shows that paid leave improves employee retention, reduces turnover, increases morale, and strengthens workforce participation. **For Memphis,__that matters.__** We want to attract talented professionals to public service. We want employees to build careers here. We want to reduce attrition and maintain a stable, experienced workforce capable of delivering high-quality services to our residents. Paid parental leave helps accomplish those goals. It demonstrates that the City of Memphis is a competitive employer that understands the realities facing modern working families. It signals that city government is committed to policies that support employees throughout all stages of life and values the people who dedicate their careers to serving Memphis. Taking care of the people who take care of Memphis _is just common sense._ **Fiscal Responsibility & Economic Stability** This policy is also about economic stability. When families have access to paid leave, they are better positioned to maintain financial security during a major life transition. That stability benefits not only individual households but our local economy as a whole. Paid parental leave is especially important for retaining women in the workforce. Research has found that access to paid leave can increase labor force participation among mothers and strengthen long-term workforce attachment. Family-friendly workplace policies help ensure that talented employees are not forced to choose between career advancement and growing their families. Importantly, investing in employees upfront can save taxpayer dollars over time. Employee turnover carries significant costs, including recruiting, hiring, onboarding, and training replacements. Retaining experienced employees is often the more fiscally responsible approach. **Setting the Right Benchmark** Research and policy expertsincreasingly point to _**twelve weeks of paid parental leave**_ as a meaningful benchmark for supporting healthy child development, family well-being, and workforce stability. Twelve weeks also corresponds with the maximum amount of unpaid, job-protected leave available to eligible employees under the federal _Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA)_ , and many family policy organizations view it as an important standard for supporting parents during the critical early months of a child's life. Local governments have an opportunity to lead where federal action has been limited. By supporting working families through paid parental leave, Memphis can demonstrate that supporting families and supporting economic growth are not competing priorities. Rather, they are mutually reinforcing goals. **A Call to Action for Memphis** _**That is why we are calling on Mayor Paul Young to implement paid parental leave for City employees through executive action**_. Doing so would demonstrate Memphis's commitment to supporting working families, strengthening our workforce, and modernizing employment policies to better meet the needs of today's employees. National surveys consistently show broad bipartisan support for paid family leave policies, reflecting a growing recognition that supporting families and supporting a strong workforce go hand in hand. At its core, paid parental leave reflects the values we frequently discuss as a community: dignity, opportunity, family, and respect for working people. We ask city employees to show up for Memphis every day. __This is Memphis showing up for them.__ _**Strong families build strong cities.**_ And when we support the people who serve our city, _we strengthen Memphis for generations to come._ ** ** **Stand with Jerri to Build a Stronger Memphis** Championing common-sense, family-first policies like paid parental leave is exactly why I step up to serve Memphis _every single day._ But to keep fighting for working families, competitive public service jobs, and a stronger local economy, we need to be able to reach further, and to do that, _**I need your help.**_ Progress doesn't happen on its own— _it requires a community standing together._ If you believe that supporting the people who serve our city strengthens Memphis for generations to come, please consider making a contribution to our campaign today. subject: RE: the Trump Administration’s attack on healthcare workers
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jasmine Clark for Georgia
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260609-nurse-rs [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260609-nurse-rs]
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260609-nurse-rs [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260609-nurse-rs]
As a professor at Emory’s nursing school, I’ve dedicated my career to training the next generation of nurses — the people who will care for us when we’re sick, deliver our babies, respond to emergencies, and literally save our lives.
So I was outraged when I saw the Trump Administration’s latest attack on healthcare workers:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260609-nurse-rs [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260609-nurse-rs]
Trump’s Department of Education has reclassified nursing as not a professional degree, slashing federal loan access for advanced nursing degrees nationwide.
Let me say that again: They are telling nurses—NURSES—that their work isn’t “professional” enough to deserve the same support as dentists, veterinarians, chiropractors, optometrists, and theologians.
But it’s not just about a title. The actual consequences will be devastating:
→ Graduate nursing students will lose access to the federal loans they need to become nurse practitioners, nurse anesthetists, midwives, and clinical specialists.
→ Nationwide nursing shortages will grow worse.
→ And patients — the people who rely on nurses the most — will pay the price.
This is a direct attack on the health care workforce. And it’s one more reminder why we need scientists, educators, and health care professionals IN Congress — not politicians who don’t understand (or don’t care about) the consequences of their actions.
I’m running for Congress because I’ve seen what happens when politicians who know nothing about medicine make decisions that endanger patients and disrespect the healthcare workers who keep this country running. But I can’t fight this fight alone. So please, will you donate $10, $25, or whatever you can to help me win this race and bring a fresh and needed perspective to Congress? Dr. Jasmine Clark

Dear Peter,
I’d like to tell you why I’m endorsing Effie Phillips-Staley’s campaign for Congress.
I've watched a lot of candidates run in tough districts. Most play it safe: they water down their message, take the corporate PAC money, and hope nobody notices they don't stand for anything. Effie is doing the opposite.
DONATE [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rk-effie-phillips-staley-fundraising-split?refcode=20260609]
Effie is running to flip NY-17, a seat held by Trump-aligned Mike Lawler. He is one of the most vulnerable Republicans in the country. And she's doing it on a platform that actually matches the scale of the problems we face:
* Medicare for All, because no one should go bankrupt for getting sick.
* A plan to build 5 MILLION new homes, because the housing crisis won't be solved with tax credits and half-measures.
* Banning hedge funds from buying single-family homes, because Wall Street shouldn't be your landlord.
And she's doing all of this without a dime of corporate PAC or AIPAC money. Effie can't be bought, and she won't be bullied into moderating a message that voters are hungry for.
Her primary is just a few weeks away, on June 23. This is the moment where grassroots support decides whether a real progressive makes it through. I've seen races like this won and lost in the final weeks. It always comes down to whether people show up.
Will you show her your support by splitting a donation between Effie's campaign and mine right now? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rk-effie-phillips-staley-fundraising-split?refcode=20260609]
DONATE [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rk-effie-phillips-staley-fundraising-split?refcode=20260609]
Thank you for your support, your activism, and all that you do.
In solidarity,
Ro

# Hanks for Colorado
Ron Hanks * Conservative Republican * US House of Representatives - District 3 * June 30 Primary
⏱ 24 days until the June 30 primary. Ballots arrive in less than a week.
My name is Ron Hanks. I'm a 32-year military veteran -- enlisted Arabic linguist, commissioned intelligence officer, deployed to Iraq, Kuwait, and Kazakhstan.
I'm not a New York lawyer. I'm not funded or managed by DC insiders.
I'm running because Western Colorado deserves a true-conservative congressman who actually shows up.
Jeff Hurd skipped a Grand Junction town hall where 400 constituents waited. He co-sponsored a Federal Land Grab with Democrat Senators Hickenlooper and Bennet that locked up 730,000 acres in our district. And he earned a [Heritage Action score of just 59% — an F-rated conservative](https://us.list-manage.com/WIf5w0wyDJM?e=934ceb4302&c2id=da2928b2c320b279d8055a9f9a66d543) -- a full 26 points below the average House Republican.
Trump called him a **" RINO Congressman who let America down."** The scorecard proves he was right.
59%
Hurd's Heritage Action score — F Rating
−26 pts
26 pts below avg House Republican
When it came time to censure anti-American Representative Ilhan Omar, Hurd was one of only 4 Republicans who voted to block it. The motion failed 214-213\. One vote. **His vote.**
See exactly how Ron and Jeff compare on every issue that matters to CD3:
[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/13Hu9QCJLQ5?e=934ceb4302&c2id=da2928b2c320b279d8055a9f9a66d543) | [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/GUbthEK3V0s?e=934ceb4302&c2id=da2928b2c320b279d8055a9f9a66d543) [Click to see Hurd's full scorecard ->](https://us.list-manage.com/tS3l61OCnEW?e=934ceb4302&c2id=da2928b2c320b279d8055a9f9a66d543)
---|---
Hear directly from Ron -- and help him fight back:
[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/m0JmiwTtsql?e=934ceb4302&c2id=da2928b2c320b279d8055a9f9a66d543)
▶ Watch Ron's message ->
Colorado's Congressional District 3 deserves a congressman who does what's right, not what handlers tell him. A congressman who will fight the hard left, not shelter them from accountability. A congressman who has believed in and fought for this country for more than 32 years and will show up ready to fight every day.
We are a grassroots, locally funded campaign. We wouldn't have it any other way. And we have a VERY GOOD opportunity to dump a campaign funded by Big Money and Outside Lobbies on its head. THEY spend MILLIONS on their LIAR FLYERS, dumped into mailboxes 5 days a week, trying to fool your neighbors that Left is Right, Wrong is Right, and that 59% is a "solid conservative". Say it ain't so, Jeff.

WE ask for 20 bucks from you -- our neighbors and Colorado citizens -- to spread the truth, and to talk about COLORADO's priorities, not Washington DC's.
**Two things you can do right now:**
1\. Chip in $10, $25, or $50 -- every dollar funds direct voter contact in these final 24 days.
2\. Forward this email to five people in CD3 who want real conservative representation.
[Chip in for Ron ->](https://us.list-manage.com/qNfapKN1kIy?e=934ceb4302&c2id=da2928b2c320b279d8055a9f9a66d543) Forward to a friend
For Colorado,

clean_body: | | | | Hey, it’s Rob Sand with some great news: I’m officially the Democratic nominee for Governor of Iowa. The other big development? I’ll face Republican Zach Lahn in the general election. If you’re thinking, “Who?” allow me to enlighten you. Zach Lahn presents himself as some kind of outsider despite being aligned with (or even MORE extreme than) Kim Reynolds in basically every way that counts. Yet he’s trying to convince us that the solution to ten years of failed one-party rule is... four more years of one-party rule. Clearly, there’s an extraordinary amount at stake in this election, and it’s really, really important that we come out on top in November, so I’ll pop the question: | | I’ve been traveling to all 99 counties every year since I ran for Auditor back in 2017. There’s one thing EVERYBODY — Democrat, Republican, independent, etc. — can agree on: the status quo is failing the majority of Iowans. We’re in the grips of a generational farm crisis, mass layoffs, education cuts, rising cancer rates, rural hospital closures, brain drain, and an economy that is now the worst in the country. These are real problems that affect real people. Meanwhile, Zach Lahn is palling around with Steve King and fighting radicalism in fifth-grade math textbooks. 🙄 Iowans are fighting an uphill battle just to make ends meet. They’re tired, and tired of fighting. It’s time to leave the culture wars behind. This race is a toss-up, according to the experts at Cook Political Report, because we’ve built one of the broadest bipartisan coalitions in American politics. That’s why the choice we face in this election is so much more than (D) or (R). It’s between a divisive culture warrior or a proven public servant who brings people together. I believe Iowans will see the contrast, but winning requires us to be realistic about the challenges we’re facing. This race is wide open. The political winds are unpredictable. subject: I know it’s cheesy

body:
I feel so loved.
#

Hello friends — Gabby Giffords here.
As you might’ve heard, it was my birthday yesterday. I wanted to take a minute and say THANK YOU! Thank you for all the birthday wishes. I feel so loved.
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q22026.A9rDp6&refcode=em260609-1-b&t=1&akid=11537%2E3935704%2E3461Fs)
I know I’m not supposed to share my wish, but I can’t help it. **I wish to continue our progress to make our communities even safer from gun violence.**
I know it’s cheesy, but I’m serious.
When GIFFORDS was founded, a majority of elected officials didn’t dare to touch the issue of guns. They said it was “political poison.”
We changed that narrative.
Over the past decade, you have helped us put the NRA on defense and pass lifesaving legislation across the country — 820 gun safety laws and counting!
That’s only been possible because of people like you — stepping up and saying enough is enough. _Thank you_.
But you and I both know there’s more work to do. As we near the midterm elections, we must continue to take on these tough fights and raise our voices. For our children, for our communities, and for our country.
I’m so grateful for your commitment in this fight.
Onward,
Gabby Giffords

**Hello! Before you scroll away — can you help us make Gabby’s birthday even more special?**
June officially marks the end of the quarter and one of the most important FEC deadlines before the November elections.
The Trump administration is working hand-in-hand with the gun lobby to undo our progress every day, including pushing to allow guns to ship through the USPS and reversing the “gun show loophole.”
We must turn up the pressure. While Donald Trump relies on wealthy, far-right billionaires to power his campaign, we’re counting on folks like you — chipping in just a few bucks at a time.
[**If you’re able, we’d appreciate it if you can pitch in a contribution to help Gabby continue the fight. Our average gift is around $25 — but any amount you can spare makes a difference in our fight for gun safety.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q22026.A9rDp6&refcode=em260609-1-b&t=2&akid=11537%2E3935704%2E3461Fs)

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | In a surprising twist, in a shocking statement that’s taking the world by storm. #
Peter,
The New York Democratic primary is only two weeks from today — **which means we have just 14 days left to elect Justice Democrat Claire Valdez in NY-07’s crowded race.**
**[Every dollar we raise between now and then makes a difference. If you’re already with us, rush a split donation right now to help power this grassroots campaign through the primary>>](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260609-cv.Mve5hY&refcode=em20260609-37885&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=37885%2E1203867%2EjP6-1v)**

[ stdin# ]Our Revolution Logo

Peter Willis,

Massive data centers are being proposed at breakneck speed across the
country — and communities are fighting back.

Big Tech profits are not worth the utter devastation these facilities
cause: thousands of acres, millions of gallons of water, sky-high utility
bills, scarce water for drinking and farming, and so much more.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39049?source=email-20260609&t=1011&akid=10861%2E5885482%2EZvDh3N ]Headline: Majority of US's new AI datacenters to be built on

just passed the country’s first-ever ban on data centers – by a landslide
86%. In Ohio, the Republican governor slammed the brakes on new tax breaks
for these billion-dollar projects.

While AI-funded politicians from both parties try to claim these
water-hogging, power-thirsty facilities mean jobs and prosperity, we’re
working to shut them down. Our Revolution is organizing side by side with
local advocates where these facilities threaten to move in, and this week

#### _**[Endless Urgency is always free to read, but this community only grows because people choose to invest in it. Every subscription helps us reach further, build something lasting, and keep these urgent conversations alive. We'd love to have you with us. Just $8/month makes a huge difference:](https://substack.com/redirect/52b70a0f-289e-4e11-ad22-9d6fd6fda475?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/52b70a0f-289e-4e11-ad22-9d6fd6fda475?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
There is a jealousy at the heart of Donald Trump and the MAGA movement that I find endlessly fascinating. More than anything else, they crave cultural relevance. They want to be seen as cool, influential, and admired in the broader culture, but the conservative movement in this country simply doesn't have that kind of juice--because they're dorks.
And that's why Trump and his movement feel the need to insert themselves into everything.
Yesterday, Trump went to the NBA Finals to see the Knicks. The Knicks were on an incredible run, and there were a bunch of genuinely fun storylines surrounding the team. As a sports fan, I've especially enjoyed the story of a professional wrestler named Danhausen whose character is a demon that can curse people and who supposedly "uncursed" the Knicks before their winning streak. Sports are fun because of weird little stories like that.
But Trump couldn't just let the day belong to the teams and the fans. The most corrupt and least popular president I've seen in my lifetime needed to make himself part of the story. And the result was predictable. Instead of the focus being on the game, the attention shifted to Trump. Security became a massive operation. Fans dealt with additional disruptions. The conversation became about him, and the Knicks lost, I would argue, in part because of that.
There he was, sitting behind layers of security and glass, eating French fries and pretending to be part of a culture that has never really embraced him.
When cameras showed him, he got booed. As he should be.
People are angry. They're angry because he promised to make life more affordable and failed. He promised to challenge the corrupt Washington establishment and became the corrupt Washington establishment. He promised transparency. He promised to release the Epstein files. He promised not to drag the country into another forever war. Instead, people look around and see rising costs, political chaos, regressive and hateful politics, and a president more interested in his own wild fancies than solving problems.
Which brings me back to the cultural relevance issue.
It wasn't that long ago that Barack and Michelle Obama showed up at the NBA All-Star Game and received overwhelming applause. And that's the kind of thing that drives Trump absolutely crazy. He wants that admiration. He wants people to genuinely love him the way they love figures who have earned public respect.
But the difference is that admiration for Trump has to be manufactured.
He gets it on friendly media outlets like Fox News. He gets it from cabinet members who seem obligated to praise him every time a camera is present. He gets it in controlled environments where criticism is unwelcome. But when he enters spaces that aren't built around him, reality tends to intrude.
That's why the boos bother him so much.
For all of Trump's wealth and power, he's never escaped the fact that what he's always wanted to be is a respected New York socialite and cultural figure. He wants the acceptance. He wants the invitations. He wants to be viewed as one of the people who matter.
And despite becoming president twice, he still can't reach what he actually wants.
The same thing is true of the broader MAGA movement. They're constantly fighting culture wars because they're obsessed with cultural relevance. They're angry about movies, television shows, athletes, celebrities, corporations, and social media trends. They're perpetually upset that the culture keeps moving in directions they don't like.
####
* * *

Just $8/month makes a huge difference:](https://substack.com/redirect/52b70a0f-289e-4e11-ad22-9d6fd6fda475?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/52b70a0f-289e-4e11-ad22-9d6fd6fda475?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
Whether it's complaining about LGBTQ representation, declaring war on entertainment companies, or insisting they're about to create a parallel culture that will replace the existing one, the pattern is always the same. They're trying to force cultural influence into existence, and it isn't happening (ask Spencer Pratt!).
But influence doesn't work that way.
People gravitate toward ideas, movements, artists, and leaders who create something compelling. What strikes me about MAGA is how little it actually creates. There's no real vision for the future. No inspiring idea about how to improve people's lives. No serious plan for expanding opportunity or improving economic security for ordinary people.
Instead, the movement is largely built around grievance, nostalgia, and resentment. It wants to drag the country backward to an imagined past while offering very little for the future.
And that's why so much of it feels hollow.
The truth is that cultural relevance can't be demanded. It can't be legislated. It can't be forced through outrage campaigns or social media algorithms. People either connect with what you're offering or they don't.
That's why Trump getting booed at a major sporting event matters more than many of his supporters would like to admit. It represents the gap between how he sees himself and how much of the public sees him.
So if you're angry about the state of the country today, remember this: Donald Trump is probably far more bothered by those boos than he'll ever publicly admit. Because beneath all the power, all the money, and all the constant demands for attention is someone who desperately wants admiration and still can't figure out why he isn't getting it.
And eventually, we have to move beyond all of this. We have to get back to solving actual problems instead of feeding one man's ego. We have to focus on making life more affordable, expanding opportunity, and building a future people can believe in.
That's the work that matters. And it's the work waiting for us once this era finally comes to an end.

name: Matias, United We Dream
subject: This is how a movement grows
body:
We’re empowering the next generation of organizers to build the skills to win concrete improvements in our lives. Donate to help us keep growing. | | | Peter, When Ale was a junior in college, she sought what many of us look for: community. Specifically, a community that understood her experience as a DACA recipient. She found United We Dream, and what began as a simple texting shift quickly turned into an unexpected journey. In her words: _"I started my relationship with UWD by helping with texting. Then, this opened the door for me to attend the Undocumented Summit in New Mexico. The Undoc Summit helped me build relationships with both staff and members, who are now like family.

Since then, I have been able to attend training events in San Francisco and New York. Along with a canvassing opportunity in Arizona. I have cherished these moments not only because of the experience, but because of the incredible relationships and feeling of belonging that they have provided."_ **Ale's story is exactly why we do this work—and why we recently brought leaders together for our Mass Movement Building: Train the Trainers gathering.** **[United We Dream is an organizing home for young leaders nationwide. This is where the next generation builds the skills to return to their communities, organize their neighbors, and win the change our communities need. Donate to help us keep growing. | | | Peter, When Ale was a junior in college, she sought what many of us look for: community. In her words: "I started my relationship with UWD by helping with texting. Then, this opened the door for me to attend the Undocumented Summit in New Mexico. The Undoc Summit helped me build relationships with both staff and members, who are now like family. Since then, I have been able to attend training events in San Francisco and New York. Along with a canvassing opportunity in Arizona. I have cherished these moments not only because of the experience, but because of the incredible relationships and feeling of belonging that they have provided." Peter,

In a heated exchange between Donald Trump and NBC’s “Meet the Press” host Kristen Welker, Trump pushed his conspiracy theories that the 2020 election was stolen. When she asked if he had evidence, he stated, “All I have to do is look.” He quickly became agitated, calling her either “crooked” or “stupid,” and refused to finish the scheduled interview. # [Americans slash tips amid "ridiculous" tipping culture backlash](https://substack.com/redirect/0c9501dd-a7cf-4f6a-bd29-e10a775ea46b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Americans have reached a breaking point with tipping demands spreading to coffee shops, takeout and apps, as a new survey shows **[78 percent now call the culture ridiculous](https://substack.com/redirect/b97c9d9b-9bd9-44ca-a619-8388832282d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and 44 percent are tipping less this year amid budget pressures.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0c9501dd-a7cf-4f6a-bd29-e10a775ea46b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Tipping Fatigue Hits Restaurants** : Thirty-five percent of respondents reduced tips when dining out, the hardest-hit sector, while **["only 41 percent now tip servers 20 percent or more, down from 45 percent last year."](https://substack.com/redirect/b97c9d9b-9bd9-44ca-a619-8388832282d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* **Digital Prompts Fuel Resentment** : Nearly three-quarters noticed restaurants raising suggested tip amounts on screens, though pressure to tip has fallen from 66 percent six months ago to 59 percent.
* **Unwarranted Tips Spending Drops** : Consumers spent an estimated $130 on gratuities they felt were unnecessary over the past year, down from $150 previously.
* **Higher Prices Preferred Option** : More than half would accept increased menu prices if it meant better wages for workers and an end to tipping expectations altogether.

# [Tim Walz ignored Minnesota fraud warnings over fears of racism](https://substack.com/redirect/0c9501dd-a7cf-4f6a-bd29-e10a775ea46b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A House Oversight report concludes Governor Tim Walz and Attorney General Keith Ellison **[knew of systemic fraud in federally funded social programs](https://substack.com/redirect/4369266f-fde8-4c6b-8951-bbeddcde6016?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** since 2019 but took no action due to fears of lawsuits and racism accusations.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0c9501dd-a7cf-4f6a-bd29-e10a775ea46b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Fraud Cost Billions** : An estimated $300 million in child nutrition funds was lost, with up to $9 billion in Medicaid spending at serious risk.
* **Political Fears Cited** : Officials reversed funding denials for Feeding Our Future sites within 24 hours after discrimination lawsuit threats and warnings not to target Somali-run providers.
* **Whistleblowers Retaliated** : Nearly 30 employees reported being ignored, surveilled or threatened, with the criminal investigations unit shut down entirely.
* **Walz Responses Vary** : The governor gave inconsistent accounts of when he learned of the fraud, wrongly cited court orders and later said he would not seek re-election to fix issues.

* * *
* * *
# [San Francisco voters reject executive tax hike measure](https://substack.com/redirect/0c9501dd-a7cf-4f6a-bd29-e10a775ea46b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
San Francisco voters defeated Measure D, which would have raised taxes on large companies with highly paid executives by expanding the CEO pay ratio formula, with 53.64 percent opposed according to election results.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0c9501dd-a7cf-4f6a-bd29-e10a775ea46b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Measure D Falls Short** : The ballot proposal needed only a simple majority but failed 46.36 percent in favor, viewed as a win for business groups.
* **Revenue Projection Significant** : City officials estimated the tax would have generated between $250 million and $300 million annually for services and income inequality efforts.
* **Tech Leaders Opposed Strongly** : Google co-founder Sergey Brin donated $500,000 to the campaign against the measure.
* **Voters Shift Centrist** : The outcome reflects a broader move toward moderate economic policies after recent recalls and the election of Mayor Daniel Lurie focused on recovery.

# [Bitcoin sell-off sparks flurry of related stock trades](https://substack.com/redirect/0c9501dd-a7cf-4f6a-bd29-e10a775ea46b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Bitcoin fell below $60,000 for the first time since October 2024 before rebounding, **[triggering heavy options activity](https://substack.com/redirect/97e3b9e5-d5ff-43cd-b6f5-84159b8c6016?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in Strategy and Coinbase stocks despite its 27 percent year-to-date loss.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0c9501dd-a7cf-4f6a-bd29-e10a775ea46b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Strategy Bearish Diagonal** : One trader sold 29,425 August 125/180-call diagonals collecting $56 million, profiting if shares stay below $125.
* **Coinbase Bullish Diagonal** : Another trader spent $21 million on a June-to-August call strategy betting the stock rises above $183.40 by August.
* **IBIT ETF Popular** : The iShares Bitcoin Trust ranked among top 20 options tickers by volume on Monday.
* **Tom Lee Comments** : BitMine chairman and FundStrat head cited bitcoin's proof-of-work resilience against AI narratives undermining traditional systems.

# [Fidelity slashes SpaceX minimum to $2,000 for retail](https://substack.com/redirect/0c9501dd-a7cf-4f6a-bd29-e10a775ea46b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Fidelity **[lowered the minimum investment for SpaceX shares](https://substack.com/redirect/83349f3f-045a-4832-8ee9-7e67ab750537?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to $2,000 for retail brokerage customers as the company reserves up to 30 percent of the offering for everyday investors.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0c9501dd-a7cf-4f6a-bd29-e10a775ea46b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Lower Bar For Access** : The reduced threshold applies specifically to this SpaceX IPO and is not a permanent policy change for other offerings.
* **Flipping Rule Enforced** : Selling shares within the first 15 calendar days after trading begins labels investors as flippers with escalating penalties.
* **Penalties Escalate Quickly** : First offense blocks future IPOs for six months, second for one year and third triggers a lifetime ban tied to SSN.
* **Allocation Limited** : Retail shares remain capped, and early sales still possible but trigger the Fidelity-specific restrictions.

# [Weight loss drug stock sinks 23 percent on disappointing safety data](https://substack.com/redirect/0c9501dd-a7cf-4f6a-bd29-e10a775ea46b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Zealand Pharma **[shares plummeted as much as 23 percent](https://substack.com/redirect/3347cd6c-5714-412e-93ec-24cd7b0ce4be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after late-stage data on survodutide showed 19 percent of patients dropped out due to gastrointestinal events versus 2.9 percent on placebo.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0c9501dd-a7cf-4f6a-bd29-e10a775ea46b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Discontinuation Rate High** : More than 40 percent reported vomiting, raising tolerability concerns despite meeting weight loss targets of up to 16.6 percent.
* **Analysts Disappointed** : Barclays called safety and tolerability disappointing, while Citi noted rates sit well above commercially viable levels versus rivals.
* **Stock Performance Hit** : Shares ended 22.7 percent lower and are down nearly 50 percent year-to-date.
* **Market Competition Intense** : Zealand partners with Boehringer Ingelheim and Roche in a field dominated by Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly products.

# [Apple debuts Siri AI with improved intelligence](https://substack.com/redirect/0c9501dd-a7cf-4f6a-bd29-e10a775ea46b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Apple **[unveiled its biggest update to Siri at WWDC,](https://substack.com/redirect/8bf7a075-196b-4b54-8bd7-256bf4095846?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** turning the assistant into a conversational AI hub powered by Google's Gemini model for back-and-forth tasks across iPhone, iPad and Mac.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0c9501dd-a7cf-4f6a-bd29-e10a775ea46b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Conversational Upgrades** : New Siri handles ongoing chats, reminders, photo searches and questions about Messages without scrolling.
* **Mac Spotlight Integration** : Users can highlight files and ask Siri to compare them or draft emails via prompts.
* **Dedicated App Added** : Conversations sync across devices with customizable voice options and camera access for nutritional info or bill splitting.
* **Writing Tools Included** : Siri can generate or critique documents from user prompts.

subject: Abbott’s only concern is protecting his power and making his wealthy donors happy
body:
Texans are being betrayed by Abbott.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
Greg Abbott has made it clear that protecting his own power matters more to him than protecting Texans.
Year after year, Abbott has doubled down on policies that benefit his biggest donors and political allies while everyday Texans pay the price.
He’s slashed funding for public schools, pushed culture wars instead of real solutions, and funneled taxpayer dollars to corporations and his own campaign donors. Meanwhile, hard-working Texans are struggling to afford groceries, healthcare, and child care, and classrooms are overcrowded and under-resourced.
The consequences of Abbott’s poor leadership are already here.
* Texas ranks near the bottom nationally in healthcare access and education.
* Millions of children have lost Medicaid coverage.
* Public schools are closing or losing millions in funding.

**Peter, when leaders choose power over people, it’s our kids who suffer — not just today, but for generations to come.**
It’s obvious that Abbott’s grip on power is costing Texans.
But Gina is running to change that — to invest in kids, strengthen public schools, expand access to healthcare, and build a Texas where families can thrive.

subject: NYT: Trump’s Push for Election Power Raises Fears He Will ‘Subvert’ Midterms
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
We’re hearing reports that President Donald Trump is considering an executive order declaring a so-called “emergency” to seize greater federal authority over elections.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
FIGHT BACK [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
This is deeply alarming to say the least.
But you don’t have to take my word for it: Our founders were explicit about this. They had just fought a king. They understood that concentrating too much power in one person was dangerous. That’s why the Constitution divides authority and states administer elections.
That’s why no president — no matter how loud or how desperate — gets to override the system because he’s afraid of losing.
As Oregon’s Secretary of State, I oversee our elections. I take an oath to the Constitution — not to any president. And I will stand up to any administration that tries to abuse emergency powers to interfere with Oregon’s voting systems or intimidate our election workers.
But I need your help to keep up the fight in light of Trump’s illegal actions, which is why I’m reaching out today. Can I count on you to join me in this fight against President Trump’s lawlessness by chipping in $5, $10, or more right away? Communicating this threat to Oregonians statewide requires resources. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]

subject: These ballot measures are a cruel attack on LGBTQ+ kids
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
On Wednesday, June 17th, I’ll be speaking at No Hate In WA State’s campaign kickoff rally.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260609-6328-footer&t=1&akid=6328%2E420207%2EPHJKwP)
Peter,
I’m proud that Washington state has a strong record of protecting the rights of LGBTQ+ kids. But this November, voters are going to have to step up and make sure that record continues.
**That’s because a MAGA megadonor has personally bankrolled the effort to get two poorly written initiatives on the ballot that would put kids at risk. Here’s how:**
* **IL26-001** would force teachers and school counselors to out LGBTQ+ kids to their families — even when it might not be safe, and including to parents who are under criminal investigation for abusing their own children. It would strip away the confidential protections that allow kids facing depression, sexual assault, domestic violence, and bullying to seek help from trusted adults, and it will undoubtedly make the teen mental health crisis even worse.
* **IL26-638** would subject girls — and only girls — to invasive genital exams to “certify” their sex before they can play school sport. Boys are completely exempt. This is the most extreme measure of its kind in the country, and it is designed to humiliate trans kids and drive them away from sports.

These measures are a cruel attack on every young person in Washington who deserves to grow up safe, supported, and free to be who they are. And I refuse to let hate win.
That’s why on Wednesday, June 17th, I’ll be speaking at No Hate In WA State’s campaign kickoff rally as they begin their work to defeat these dangerous initiatives. And I hope I can count on you to support their work, too.
[**If you can, please consider splitting a donation between my campaign and No Hate In WA State today. We’re going to need all the help we can get to oppose these MAGA initiatives and continue standing up for LGBTQ+ rights.**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260609.naINXZ&refcode=em20260609-6328&amount=3&t=2&akid=6328%2E420207%2EPHJKwP)

In solidarity,

| | **Summer Camp** Generations For America Foundation is proud to collaborate with Jean's Angel this summer for an exciting six-week summer camp program for students of all ages from June 15, 2026 through July 20, 2026. We will be teaching children to improve their print and cursive writing during their 6 week summer camp and we are looking for volunteers who want to help us promote 250 years of American history through instruction from 10 a.m. to 11 a.m. three times a week starting on Monday, 6/15/26. A patriotic coloring book will be given to the children to learn U.S. history. Generations For America Foundation will provide one hour of penmanship instruction while teaching the United States Constitution and American history. We are excited to help children improve their print writing skills while also learning the art of cursive handwriting. Generations For America Foundation is dedicated to promoting civic literacy, American history, and penmanship education for all ages.

clean_body: Volunteer to help kids learn history and have fun | | | | Help Teach Colorful American History and Penmanship! | | | | | Summer Camp Generations For America Foundation is proud to collaborate with Jean's Angel this summer for an exciting six-week summer camp program for students of all ages from June 15, 2026 through July 20, 2026. We will be teaching children to improve their print and cursive writing during their 6 week summer camp and we are looking for volunteers who want to help us promote 250 years of American history through instruction from 10 a.m. to 11 a.m. three times a week starting on Monday, 6/15/26. A patriotic coloring book will be given to the children to learn U.S. history. Generations For America Foundation will provide one hour of penmanship instruction while teaching the United States Constitution and American history. We are excited to help children improve their print writing skills while also learning the art of cursive handwriting. Generations For America Foundation is dedicated to promoting civic literacy, American history, and penmanship education for all ages. | | | | | | | | | Volunteers Throughout the week, music will be used as an educational tool to improve penmanship and student engagement. America’s founding documents were written in cursive — an important art form that is slowly disappearing, yet remains essential for reading historical documents and strengthening literacy skills. If you would like to volunteer this summer, please contact us immediately. We are happy to provide meaningful service opportunities and community service hours to keep students and volunteers engaged. Volunteers will meet at 956 South Live Oak, Moncks Corner, SC 29461 from 10 am to 11:30 AM daily. Peter, I wanted to share a story with you about what makes this time of year so important. It was only recently that my hometown had its first ever Pride Parade, and a conversation with one young man was particularly special, and will stay with me for a long time. He said to me, “You came to my school as our weatherman and I knew you were gay and you helped me be myself. When I saw you run for Congress and win? I knew I wanted to follow in your footsteps!” **THAT, Peter, means as much to me as anything. As wise trailblazers before me have said, "You can't be what you can't see."** I love celebrating Pride Month with events and parades, but stories like this one shows that this time of year is about the generations of children in Illinois who will see themselves represented in their own hometowns, whoever they are. **Every young child deserves to know that they can be themselves and still thrive – and lead – in our communities.** Talking to that young man, I saw the next generation of Rockford leaders. **I am so proud to be Illinois’ first openly out Member of Congress, and I am going to work tirelessly to make sure I am not the last.** That starts with our re-election this November. [**We need to hold this seat to continue making our community better for ALL of our neighbors, and that means raising enough to fend off extremist, often bigoted attacks. After my time in the Marine Corps, I returned to my hometown and set out to serve the community that raised me. I became a pastor at my local church and eventually became mayor. I was blessed with every opportunity to serve my community, to make the world a better place.

My job title changed, but the core values that I live my life by never did. I believe in these principles with every fiber of my being: Faith. Discipline. Integrity. Patriotism.

name: Tim Walz
subject: I know what it means, Peter

body:
If Democrats want to win in more places, we’ve got to start showing up in more places.
#
Peter,
I grew up in a small town.
I know what it means when people treat places like that as an afterthought. A dot on a map. A place to drive through. A place to fly over.
_But small towns are not flyover country._
They are home to teachers, veterans, laborers, nurses, small business owners, young people, parents, grandparents, farmers, and neighbors trying to build a good life in the places they love.
When Democrats stop showing up in communities like these, somebody else fills the void — politicians, tech bros, and billionaires who divide working families, distract from the real problems, and cash in while our neighbors get left behind.
**I started Small Town PAC to help Democrats show up in places too many people have written off, organize with the folks who call these communities home, and build the power we need to expand the map.**
[**We’re going to help Democrats compete in more places, support leaders who actually know their communities, and make the case everywhere. Will you make a contribution of $5 today to help us do it?**](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260609-1.YKW9f0&amount=5&refcode=em20260609-743&t=2&akid=743%2E34582%2EVqUH0q)

I’m grateful,
Tim Walz

| | Peter,
---
I want to give you a picture of what's really happening right now -- not the polished version, but what it actually looks like on the ground.

Inside our office, tables are covered in supplies and open boxes. Coworkers are coming together, packing materials, sealing kits, and sending them out the door as fast as possible.
---
[](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=a0da621572ee4a568fbcde61c37189b2&_e=kOA3Q7Njj4Q3xiUAg_FGE9_VPkT9vHSWVXMpnGwZ0sR4A3FS22ZQmS5sj8tldU-ksqwhLJvXQAEwKRxIrVKBLT_NxK5uoF0jvuhsWUSSZt7q1OmO1lGutCqPCMAZF924YB_A0m5cmOWJ3DrDyKdtzOfRlMi0SDZoMQIPaODaWysf0pmim8nJRSpK9XoNu_3ry7KL4IFBwR98wiqJb3OSgSgNEZlTt-RAg8jnem8p-fUKOMTTjEu4nTr2Oz9MQlao-xFlVT9xnsjHH84yw1yXSBmXU2WIL-DsfEK4BKblH06f02JsSZMC0ZaPDopnP_BqNXt03y-bazAAJ_b4GJUPZFJsZ18k6gJr8bfgf8H1Dkm-AaqyViERRV9GarFkoltL4r_9_8CL6YVfa2uXDn_f5tU4Sy06nOSAB3qBJGX-MDrFvt0NOFlOMOs-jPr-sgtXQ65Izg3FzkHRFlXJBGB0NMNSdCvUi0PZ3AAQ2oslS1z-1ovRcjuGlLfpPbf3GaUskwuea6Vv7JwYM4fJ7Gyu8gj81RBJj0dlJcHMRn5zZtyhQeHzMfdshnn-Nj0RJ14vR-7ywrtuL6m-vhxw8YaRI0Nsu21GAoxgbfM8R9GxWAgxqeVN8kJG64YFYiujvx8DIT0pSX8HUWdij0I5Vc1Gouce12rFs7WqYb-nEnTg5dXstNCH5Rv_mabv5MYzQGI8r8jcY-UC81uu7w7jeJDz5w%3D%3D)
---
_Above: Activism kits bound for new chapters being packed with Constitutions, chapter handbooks, American flags, and more at TPUSA HQ in Arizona_
---
These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them.

They're already claimed. And we don't have extras.

By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in.

Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it.

That's where things stand right now.

We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment.

And I don't say that lightly.

Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down.

The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great.

And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing.

Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back.

**We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. **

For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there.

And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet.
---
[](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=a0da621572ee4a568fbcde61c37189b2&_e=kOA3Q7Njj4Q3xiUAg_FGE9_VPkT9vHSWVXMpnGwZ0sR4A3FS22ZQmS5sj8tldU-ksqwhLJvXQAEwKRxIrVKBLT_NxK5uoF0jvuhsWUSSZt7q1OmO1lGutCqPCMAZF924YB_A0m5cmOWJ3DrDyKdtzOfRlMi0SDZoMQIPaODaWysf0pmim8nJRSpK9XoNu_3ry7KL4IFBwR98wiqJb3OSgSgNEZlTt-RAg8jnem8p-fUKOMTTjEu4nTr2Oz9MQlao-pzM268tyoZ893s-z5bpzIFDBCJRhxPqyZBTUiIH0i9-FP6DRXPL4c3a7_9K47pxCPM6gSVLCSKIVBRL_pnalNABIfuRb9X3ntqvWT6JheFYPooQScuhRrQAMyv3lZIIiIDqhqO9gjeaVywlBOSyzZU2ITUaWKBSVZqFTv3f6zsluEUi0LQv1MMgspNv4ZkgH5x7wtFeJrVJxp9Dabs9j0S4oMP19OEKAi7zi59quHw9fIFSV43Dyxd4jGJGbKc-loRWhvKzN6xwSKffwgDpJBFrdXXCpwx-_vCMG5nMbnyH2GvZiUiGQ9Bol1pF1GSZN574Qwge8Fcw2yjBM726GSkMOrrJ1GtEnqzpv3uRc6RQmL_PnBdZDWQuF1ziiEGdM6R9iONVJ8oCEYIYyS5fyW7KFpmC3a3VB-DHEIAftOqdD7ZYtqO6FO0zXpq8lscyHAL9Vuul0GEOIzHm3zvw5Q%3D%3D)
---
That's not something you can just manufacture. But it is something you can support when it happens.

And it's not isolated growth anymore.

**We 're now working with more than 1,450 college chapters and over 3,400 high school chapters across the country. That's real scale. **

But if you zoom out, there are roughly 27,000 high schools in America.

That means tens of thousands of campuses where the Left still dominates the conversation...

And where students are waiting for someone to help them stand up and speak.

So as much as this has grown, we're still in the early innings of what Charlie actually set out to build.

What's different now is the pace.

**Many states are moving to bring Club America chapters to every high school statewide, including: **

✅ Arkansas
✅ Florida
✅ Idaho
✅ Indiana
✅ Montana
✅ Nebraska
✅ Oklahoma
✅ South Carolina
✅ Texas
✅ Tennessee

That brings us to ten states now taking this seriously -- not just talk, but action.
---
[](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=a0da621572ee4a568fbcde61c37189b2&_e=kOA3Q7Njj4Q3xiUAg_FGE9_VPkT9vHSWVXMpnGwZ0sR4A3FS22ZQmS5sj8tldU-ksqwhLJvXQAEwKRxIrVKBLT_NxK5uoF0jvuhsWUSSZt7q1OmO1lGutCqPCMAZF924YB_A0m5cmOWJ3DrDyKdtzOfRlMi0SDZoMQIPaODaWysf0pmim8nJRSpK9XoNu_3ry7KL4IFBwR98wiqJb3OSgSgNEZlTt-RAg8jnem8p-fUKOMTTjEu4nTr2Oz9MQlaoK7s4BdGggVsmCE9EciS8KIvlwWzuHxdZodb3K_XNmefPpxOxNqCslLhadpFhBqE_wH6jOeXH_Te4JO7ah9cxpBlrBeKlFWgWC8ZK0qcL0wN_T1bCqwCLHuoSQzyKtLnatPCAYZ_NwDGrJE2tbV6u1bhgIM_j8MPu94OchDLgirO6zFFxxVuBuq4wBv6hnxG6DRdWReJGu7KJRUnCQNqAoCKUUgVIABXZHiiA701oiGbyqgsNA8bkWsvDcXaZmt_C-OqUsi9vGdmfMce7nGfhi1o7aQv_ZbnnVhUTojiGYnc7sqqz-9_LkFI_f-7fWzRPJQWcLrH_QpTmWhT2mmZnHpubXbfEq1PUYIp3yV93RZZdSpjtYjxXw92H5bDq9Uxd8xqfWwM9Je_qWBsOchhE-7j35BfpWI2F5b2OtOTS2Qe_vVQ2V7Z-gM56U0czMRbJCnVdwMog1pkbOq9UODpV3Q%3D%3D)
---
That kind of expansion doesn't happen slowly.

It stacks quickly -- and it creates pressure behind the scenes to keep up.

Because every new chapter, every new student leader, every new school means more materials, more support, more follow-through.

And right now, that's where we're stretched.

We're not lacking interest or momentum.

We're working to keep up with both.

_So here 's how you can help... _

Right now, there are students ready to step up -- they just need the tools to do it.

**An activism kit puts everything they need directly into their hands: **

✅ Constitutions.
✅ Chapter guides.
✅ Flags.
✅ Materials to organize and lead.

It turns a student who wants to speak up... _into one who actually does. _

And you'll make it possible for us to keep saying yes when a student reaches out and says, "I want to start something here."

**"Payback for Gavin Newsom’s Fiscal Folly"**
_By Will Swaim_ Beset on all sides by regulators, highest-in-the-nation taxes, environmentalists, identitarians, and a political establishment committed to class war, California business owners may want to send thanks and a muffin basket to Representative Vince Fong.

Fong, a Bakersfield, Calif., Republican, has introduced HR 8892, the Creating Accountability in Loan Repayment Act. CAL Repayment (you get the acronymic joke) would require states with outstanding federal unemployment-insurance debt to use future flexible federal aid to repay those loans before spending the money elsewhere.

At present, California is the only member of that club — which is why some Capitol Hill insiders call Fong’s bill the Gavin Newsom Reform Act.

Governor Newsom borrowed $20 billion in May 2020, making him the first governor to tap a Covid-era federal loan program designed to backstop losses on state unemployment insurance funds. By October of that year, 22 other governors also had received loans. But after [New York Governor Kathy Hochul](https://us.list-manage.com/12_XFFLqpAO?e=affd398937&c2id=4fd8e839bd16eef39626cb246bcc01d8) crafted a grand bargain to repay her state’s loan last summer, Newsom found himself the program’s only deadbeat.

Then came Fong.

“What was intended to be a lifeline for unemployed workers during the pandemic has now left California with more than $18 billion in unpaid federal unemployment insurance debt,” Fong said in announcing his bill.

What really ticks off Fong is that Newsom’s profligacy — his dishonesty — has injured millions of innocent others. That’s because a federal law requires employers in delinquent states to repay their states’ loans through a surcharge on federal payroll taxes. In 2022, that surcharge on California businesses was $21 per employee. The law automatically raises that surcharge by $21 per year until the debt is repaid. However painful to those businesses, the slow, reptilian squeeze of the federal surcharges doesn’t even keep pace with interest on the principal loan amount. With interest, that original $20 billion federal obligation will grow to about $23 billion by December 31. By then, the surcharge will be $105 per employee.

Everyone loses. Billions of dollars that might have gone toward wages, bonuses, capital investments, or the bottom line have flowed instead to the federal government. Fong’s CAL Repayment Act would end the madness.

_[Continue reading at at www.NationalReview.com](https://us.list-manage.com/bqvIO9GEnP4?e=affd398937&c2id=4fd8e839bd16eef39626cb246bcc01d8)_

Congressman Vince Fong

This is the game that matters most. I am honored to be in it -- and I would be humbled to have you as my teammate in this fight.

| | | |
---
| | | Hi Patriot, My name is Jay Feely. I'm a husband, a father of four, a retired NFL player, sports broadcaster, and a proud Arizona conservative -- **and I'm running for Congress in Arizona's 1st District.** I'll tell you more about my story in a moment. But first, I need you to understand what's at stake in this race -- because it goes far beyond Arizona. **AZ-1 is one of the most targeted House seats in the country in 2026.** Democrats and their allied super PACs already have this race circled. If they flip this seat, they have a path to reclaiming the House majority -- and reversing everything we've fought to build. That is why President Trump and Republican House Leadership have endorsed me in this race, [_**and why I'm writing to you today asking for your support.**_](http://links.right-red.com/u/click?_t=7f2cc7f35be547959fee68a54bdac0d9&_m=ec7c23be285e4ede9792db14b418a0be&_e=GrOkGV3TAXpyF2x4DedmSje_P4lVsHSHNwadoBNN8EHu9tSCGmjVr3xE3Mh5qW_w_DvB2-dclwuPUKeS9n7YzdUVj8d08yof3Zm8axk2SETxg9L5_4VQkoDJdrsms8sGQ-lMDA5nAbgpLDG_I0BqZULQYJl32rZeEJJ1pDFCJu7D2-IEtcmz-0XIJu13CReLgy5X1pKihJgfiZ-xaPuNp8PtF5ztlLE3cRuj1F7QkcNGmJAC6rBcTuL-rj5BYpJTtttbOx8IU_amhy3-B9d8M94DnAvl_q7kbOequCLFDir3z3D6yBAebiWhjuxK8kxzP39Q_o9wp6cWbCV21UWVW4sdS9Ryg48DVABhBUaLaxXf-YFmZMjs083uaHifY6TcSOymjwpdg8Hjhi2Jea58s5lJ9mrbM8v123ZWJkP9l6irGHHFcR7OcXrWQWak0zxz4YcdqajPCLHVzBZFTM-pHRO8BA6WYkSKpds5q14spj4tDJXmVcJ5CILE0Nfb96_wI_v-yECQEt2IoWDsptt3IjgxNNw0rcjK7hfuHfLAK2BCEHLSgbI6qgwFS6NbUkI1DgP9uyIC_hnhri_IYMfr81LTLiODvNtEzzwcO7TStH2Gi2WfW8UFxFhp_dMeWbxrnEYBiZ4kMjJMKhRXevvaty4utGM_r2uDU-EO1TJW9F1F9K7eXWAS2ZsaM5IuaebYBwEmW39nEK5wPyTJ7Trs-g%3D%3D)

Now -- let me tell you who I am and why I believe God has called me to this fight. I grew up in a middle-class family in Florida, and was taught from a young age that **our blessings aren't meant to be hoarded -- they're meant to be poured out for others.** That truth has shaped every chapter of my life. I earned a scholarship to the University of Michigan, won a National Championship in 1997, and went on to play fourteen years in the NFL. I wasn't the biggest or the fastest player on the field. But I was elected team captain on three different teams because my teammates trusted me to lead with integrity and fight for what was right.
---
[](http://links.right-red.com/u/click?_t=7f2cc7f35be547959fee68a54bdac0d9&_m=ec7c23be285e4ede9792db14b418a0be&_e=GrOkGV3TAXpyF2x4DedmSje_P4lVsHSHNwadoBNN8EHu9tSCGmjVr3xE3Mh5qW_w_DvB2-dclwuPUKeS9n7YzdUVj8d08yof3Zm8axk2SETxg9L5_4VQkoDJdrsms8sGQ-lMDA5nAbgpLDG_I0BqZULQYJl32rZeEJJ1pDFCJu7D2-IEtcmz-0XIJu13CReLgy5X1pKihJgfiZ-xaPuNp1MQ-pwPrsm_bie4T-eGJgfuYx0t6VG7YGLKzUX8K8EiEMvGZxDDxpoxlKGwqhhYvGFD8z4BP79TlFT0GIdK06fxM2JSiCslq3v48TL6giqWjhJKW4XpY4KkDcLqnzlJFRn1a9ZPKToagOcKR9kuHGCCh9acQbFKUmfOCx-pcb7o_v7ko9-Mw4Imw8wCwYwBM9GbEHkP2TqMPQ4Xq-mr3y5x6GsQ8XSRsOp_uROT56T-TVugwYmCZbpmlQPpy0JAiSRB-HGrkFej0YYeyM3b4oLHFxhL0ohrpZXTOpIDCH9eTa_sCNiziuFgs3-MgNO-UpQFPqS5f-ljWq6rNr2iArlI5vzbCml1tjPhs93_s9r9DZPN-cxqC1VlAUPl2Xq2Ywpv2MILMB_aN6rZsCkDGl11Jk6y5PT5As-aWzYM-v-crbtpgcJDMoO4rQSOX-n7nJubknrXoQEuLCGPk1a-FY-mcT9bMVqCH43VGyGFMU6-k_-wgKQMiJ88f9XBtqnZoQ%3D%3D)

When the NFL went into lockout negotiations, my fellow players sent me to Washington to sit across the table from ownership at the Federal mediation office. **I didn't back down then. I won't back down in Congress either.** After football, I spent ten years as an NFL analyst for CBS, earning five Emmy Awards along the way. But the work I'm most proud of has nothing to do with broadcast booths or trophies. My wife Rebecca and I fell in love with Arizona fifteen years ago when I signed with the Cardinals. We loved it so much we decided it was the perfect place to raise our family -- and we've been putting down roots here ever since. We founded the Feely Family Foundation to invest in youth and education. I served on the Gilbert Christian School Board. I started the first girls' soccer program at Gilbert Christian High School, coached our daughter Lexi's team to a state championship, and was named Arizona State Coach of the Year.

**_The border crisis is real_** , and it has impacted communities like ours every single day -- straining our schools, our hospitals, our law enforcement, and our neighborhoods. Our **_small business owners_** are being crushed by taxes and federal regulations that punish hard work and reward dependency. And Washington has been kicking these problems down the road for decades while the people who sent them there are left to deal with the wreckage. I have spent my life preparing for moments that matter. **This is one of those moments.** I believe God has blessed me with a platform, a voice, and a set of experiences that can make a real difference in Congress. I believe my kids -- and yours -- deserve a representative who will fight for them with everything he has. And I believe that each of us has to decide whether we're going to watch from the sidelines or get in the game when it counts. **_This is when it counts._** I am asking you -- humbly and sincerely -- to stand with me today. subject: Peter, this is un-American and unacceptable
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Dan Goldman for New York**
body:
Donald Trump has made it clear that he views due process as an obstacle rather than a constitutional requirement. |
---
Peter, This week, I spent several hours observing immigration court proceedings. What I witnessed was shocking. The Trump administration is now using what are known as “mega master hearings” — proceedings where dozens upon dozens of people, _sometimes as many as 100_ , are brought before a judge in assembly-line fashion. That’s not due process — it’s a factory. People are being processed through the system as quickly as possible, one after another, with little regard for their individual situations that our laws require. _This is disgraceful. body:
House Democrats passed the War Powers Resolution. Here is why Jahana voted yes — and why she needs you with her now. | | Friend, This month, House Democrats voted to end Trump’s reckless war in Iran. The vote passed 215 to 208. Out of 218 House Republicans, only four stood up to Trump. _Only four._ **Jahana Hayes voted yes.** For months, the President has violated the Constitution by engaging in conflict with Iran. This unnecessary war has cost the lives of American troops. It has driven up energy costs, disrupted supply chains, and deepened concern about domestic security and division at home. The war is widely unpopular — _**60 percent**_**of American adults disapprove of the conflict.** By passing the resolution, the House moved to force the President to adhere to the Constitution, which requires that troops be withdrawn within 60 days unless Congress authorizes continued action. _This is a critical check on the ability of any President to commit our armed forces to conflict without the consent of Congress._ **Jahana asserted that constitutional authority with her vote.
