_**By David Shuster**_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c22a0b04-58c3-4fe3-b0d6-bb905ba679a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The White House South Lawn has hosted state dinners, Easter egg rolls, military ceremonies, diplomatic receptions, and moments of national mourning. It has served as a backdrop for presidents addressing the nation during wars, economic crises, and historic achievements.
Now, if Donald Trump gets his way, it will host a UFC cage match.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2e25bd8c-f1ed-4bf1-9fac-c9554e214407?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The plan bears the unmistakable Trump stamp, a charlatan who decided long ago that modern politics is not the art of government but the manufacture of spectacle. Whereas earlier presidents sought to impress the citizenry with inspiring speech, intelligence, and moral purpose, Trump has always preferred the methods of a demented carnival barker. The crowd must be amused. The crowd must be astonished. The crowd must never be permitted to reflect, think for themselves, or embrace reality.
The UFC event, scheduled for June 14, is the logical destination for Trump's crass and toxic political culture and for an approach that always prioritizes shallow spectatorship. The White House, also known as the executive residence, will become a national amusement pavilion, complete with combatants battering one another for the entertainment of the multitudes gathered on the South Lawn, watching giant screens at the nearby ellipse or viewing on television. There will be a few MAGA celebrity guests, lots of television cameras, an Octagon fighting ring, and a 92 foot-tall, 600 ton temporary steel structure known as 'the claw.'
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2e25bd8c-f1ed-4bf1-9fac-c9554e214407?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
It is part of the arena structure and serves as the lighting and broadcast engineering canopy.
The UFC spectacle, with all of its various Trump White House components, has a certain grotesque symmetry. Why should a Trump government conducted as entertainment not feature an actual cage match? Why preserve even the faintest pretense that public affairs are distinct from show business? The distinction has been fading for a decade. Trump is now simply finishing the job with the assistance of UFC CEO Dana White.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2e25bd8c-f1ed-4bf1-9fac-c9554e214407?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
There are, however, some potential challenges for Trump and his UFC sycophants. Lawyers have descended upon the scheme with the enthusiasm of RFK junior approaching a roadside animal carcass.
A federal lawsuit is asking a court to rule that the people's house, without a formal act of Congress, can not lawfully be transformed into a for profit gladiatorial venue.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2e25bd8c-f1ed-4bf1-9fac-c9554e214407?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The prospect of federal judges spending their working hours pondering the constitutional dimensions of a cage match on the White House grounds is a commentary on this Trump era.
Another challenge involves mother nature.
Washington, D.C. in June is a city perpetually threatened by atmospheric insurrection. Thunderheads gather with alarming speed. Lightning flashes across the sky. Rain descends in torrents. Any resident of the capital knows that outdoor plans during the month are often written with an "indoor plan B."
For more than a decade, I lived in Georgetown, about a 10 minute walk northwest of the White House. During the course of my life and career in D.C., I lost track of the number of back patio gatherings I hosted or attended that suddenly required a mass stampede inside.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2e25bd8c-f1ed-4bf1-9fac-c9554e214407?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2e25bd8c-f1ed-4bf1-9fac-c9554e214407?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So, it is very possible that the grand White House extravaganza, after months of promotion, oceans of publicity, and a $60 million dollar production cost for the UFC, will find itself at the mercy of a thunderstorm. There would be something almost poetic in such an outcome.
Imagine the scene. Thousands assembled. Television cameras poised. The UFC combatants prepared to commence their ritual mayhem with Donald Trump watching ringside.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2e25bd8c-f1ed-4bf1-9fac-c9554e214407?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Then a distant rumble. A flash of lightning. A hurried announcement from officials advising everyone to seek shelter.
At that moment the oldest force in American life would reassert itself. Not democracy. Not constitutional government. Not public virtue. Weather.
(The latest forecast predicts zero precipitation on June 14, with a high temperature of 90 degrees Fahrenheit. So the Trumpsters may escape any challenges with rain and storms.
Trump, his supporters, and the UFC fighters may not escape the storm of problems that come with bugs, gnats, and moths.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2e25bd8c-f1ed-4bf1-9fac-c9554e214407?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
UFC CEO Dana White says he attended a White House rose garden dinner recently and was shocked by the number of flying insects.
And the swarms will only intensify thanks to the massive television lights.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2e25bd8c-f1ed-4bf1-9fac-c9554e214407?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Several UFC athletes, uncomfortable with the politics and the outdoor conditions, have already said "no thanks."
Several celebrities have also responded to the Trump and UFC invitation with a "no thanks." The irony is remarkable. Modern celebrity culture in America is built on the pursuit of relentless attention. These are people who routinely attend product launches, influencer conventions, awards ceremonies of questionable necessity, and parties whose sole purpose is to commemorate the existence of other parties.
Yet countless stars in the sports world and entertainment industries (including TV, movies, and music) have considered the prospect of a White House UFC cage fight and concluded that they would prefer not to be photographed anywhere near it.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2e25bd8c-f1ed-4bf1-9fac-c9554e214407?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2e25bd8c-f1ed-4bf1-9fac-c9554e214407?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This is no ordinary social rebuff. It is a watershed moment. To be shunned by celebrities requires effort. To be shunned by dozens of them simultaneously suggests a level of vulgarity so concentrated that even professional publicity-seekers find it overpowering.
The truly comic element is that Trump has spent a lifetime cultivating celebrity approval, celebrity proximity, and celebrity glamour. Yet here, at the very moment he seeks to transform the presidential mansion into the world's most expensive combat sports backdrop, and part of the nation's 250th birthday celebrations, even many members of the notoriously attention-hungry celebrity tribe are refusing to participate.
When actors, influencers, reality stars, and assorted professional exhibitionists begin looking around and muttering, "This seems a bit tacky," the situation has clearly gone beyond ordinary bad taste.
To be clear, the issue is not whether UFC athletes deserve respect.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2e25bd8c-f1ed-4bf1-9fac-c9554e214407?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Many are remarkable competitors. And their mixed martial arts sport is clearly popular and enjoyed by millions of Americans.
The issue is whether the grounds of the executive mansion should be a stage for televised combat spectacle, designed to generate ratings, social media buzz, and political theater.
The White House should remain a place where Americans encounter the dignity of self-government, not a crass and unprofessional commercial sports venue that only serves the vanity of Donald Trump.
If karma is alive, the swarms of moths and other annoying flying insects will be there too.

**NEW AD: Letlow Takes On Radical Left Indoctrination and Boys in Girls’ Sports** _Letlow’s new TV ad highlights her record in Congress fighting the radical left_
**BATON ROUGE, LA** — Today, Congresswoman Julia Letlow’s campaign released a new television advertisement highlighting her fight to stop the radical left from pushing its agenda on Louisiana children, parents, and families.
The ad focuses on Letlow’s leadership as the author of the Parents’ Bill of Rights and her record fighting to keep biological boys out of girls’ sports and locker rooms.
As a mother, former educator, and former athlete, Letlow has been one of the strongest conservative voices in Congress for putting parents back in charge, protecting young girls, and defending basic common sense.
_“The radical left wants to push parents out of the classroom, force its agenda on our kids, and make young girls compete against biological boys. Julia Letlow is fighting back, and she has the record to prove it,”_**said Katherine Thordahl, Letlow for Louisiana Communications Director**.
The ad is part of the campaign’s ongoing effort to highlight Letlow’s conservative record and her commitment to protecting Louisiana families, defending parents’ rights, and standing up for girls’ sports.

JULIA LETLOW:_When I talk to moms and dads, they’re fearful their children are being indoctrinated in the public school system. That’s why I authored the Parents’ Bill of Rights. These are our children, not the government’s._

body:
Here are 15 pieces of messaging advice to seize the agenda from the Trump regime

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133021703/626467361/2130526953?refcode=emwrapper&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiY2YwMWM3MDMtNTE2NC1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=NtoK0RfuMPbzkyEWPxB76aN7aWTi7EicuFVdHmqJ9yU=&emci=cb01c703-5164-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&emdi=cf01c703-5164-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&ceid=14016711)
Hi — Mark Jacob here, contributor at COURIER.
Most voters don’t spend their evenings studying policy platforms.
They absorb impressions. They remember headlines. They respond to stories, emotions, and simple messages that make sense of a complicated world.
That’s one reason Donald Trump has remained politically successful despite years of lies, scandals, and failures: he understands the power of messaging.
In this piece, I offer 15 suggestions for pro-democracy advocates heading into a midterm election that could have enormous consequences for the future of the country.
[**Before you read on, I hope you'll consider supporting COURIER. Independent journalism matters because the fight for democracy is also a fight over what stories get told and how they're told.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133021704/626467362/90330534?refcode=20260609_Mark_Jacob&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiY2YwMWM3MDMtNTE2NC1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=NtoK0RfuMPbzkyEWPxB76aN7aWTi7EicuFVdHmqJ9yU=)
Thanks for reading,
Mark Jacob
COURIER Contributor
* * *
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133021705/626467363/90330534?refcode=20260609_Mark_Jacob&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiY2YwMWM3MDMtNTE2NC1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=NtoK0RfuMPbzkyEWPxB76aN7aWTi7EicuFVdHmqJ9yU=)
Most voters do not study candidates’ position statements. They see a headline here and there, they hear what friends and relatives say, and they often make their decisions based on past practice or gut instincts – on what makes them feel good about themselves.
They like straight talk, or at least what sounds like straight talk. Trump has been lying to voters for more than a decade, but many people still think “he tells it like it is” because he’s blunt. He has shown us the importance of messaging.
Below are 15 tips for pro-democracy advocates preparing for a midterm election that may well determine whether you and your family live in a free country. Consider using them in your political activism and/or social media. Some of my advice applies to the mainstream media, too, but they’re not supposed to campaign for candidates. If only they would campaign for the truth, that would be enough for me.
**1\. Make change part of the message.**
I’m convinced that one reason Democrats lost the White House in 2024 is because they were, in essence, running to extend Joe Biden’s presidency, even after Kamala Harris took over the race. There’s a deep feeling of dissatisfaction in this country. People want change. One of the biggest mistakes Democrats could make is basing their campaigns on going back to “normal.” People don’t want to vote for the same Democrats who seem to be in the process of losing our democracy to Trumpism. To win, Democrats must trumpet a bold, new agenda. For example, there’s an illegal war going on. Oppose it.
**2\. Don’t waste time trying to crack the cult.**
Our messaging should be aimed more at past non-voters than at current Republican voters. The majority of MAGA cult members are lost to us. Getting apathetic non-voters to show up at the polls is a more achievable goal.
**3\. Don’t focus only on Trump.**
When Trump is your sole target, you do a favor to every other Republican who enables his fascism. Trump’s not actually on the ballot, and his political lackeys who are running this year will try to create distance from him before the midterms. We want people to vote against Republicans as a group. A good term to use is “Trump Republicans.”
**4\. Be a good ally.**
One of the most exasperating behaviors of progressives is to attack people who agree with them almost all of the time instead of people who always disagree with them. This is not to say you have to support awful Democrats like Chuck Schumer. But keep a firm grip on who your allies and enemies are, and treat them differently.
**5\. Keep bringing up Epstein.**
This issue has power because the regime is still covering up the truth about Trump’s former friend, sex trafficker Jeffrey Epstein. The reason to keep the Epstein scandal front and center isn’t to get right-wing extremists to vote for Democrats; it’s to get them to have such disgust with Republicans that they stay home.
**6\. Martyrs matter.**
Keep reminding people about Renee Good and Alex Pretti. Republican politicians are OK with masked government thugs murdering peaceful Americans in the streets. But the vast majority of voters are not.
**7\. Scream about Jim Crow 2.0.**
The racists on the Supreme Court and in the Republican Party have turned back the clock six decades on Black political power. If white Democrats act like it’s just political maneuvering instead of moral depravity, they won’t deserve the votes of Black people or anyone who cares about fair government.
**8\. Do not abandon trans people.**
Look at the most popular politicians today. They’re authentic. They’re not throwing marginalized Americans to the wolves in desperate attempts to curry favor with bad actors. Voters like politicians who stand for something – and who stand with people. The Republicans’ hate campaign against trans people is an attempt to distract from their indefensible positions on key issues. When they bring up trans people as a weapon, call them the bigots that they are and refocus the conversation on GOP failures.
[DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133021706/626467364/90330534?refcode=20260609_Mark_Jacob&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiY2YwMWM3MDMtNTE2NC1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=NtoK0RfuMPbzkyEWPxB76aN7aWTi7EicuFVdHmqJ9yU=)
**9-11. Choose the right words.**
Three bits of advice on framing:
* When you’re talking about the attack on abortion rights, say, “They’re taking away women’s right to control their own bodies.” Cast it as an issue of personal freedom. Which it is.
* It’s not “gun control” – it’s “gun safety measures” or even “sensible gun safety measures.”
* Call it “gay marriage” or “same-sex marriage” if you want, but “marriage equality” is better.

**12\. Highlight the most detestable Trumpers.**
Remember how Republicans used to run against Nancy Pelosi in congressional races nationwide? Democrats should do that with the worst characters in the Trump regime. In this piece, I offer 15 suggestions for pro-democracy advocates heading into a midterm election that could have enormous consequences for the future of the country. = Thanks for reading, Mark Jacob COURIER Contributor = Most voters do not study candidates’ position statements. They see a headline here and there, they hear what friends and relatives say, and they often make their decisions based on past practice or gut instincts – on what makes them feel good about themselves. If only they would campaign for the truth, that would be enough for me. 1\. Make change part of the message. I’m convinced that one reason Democrats lost the White House in 2024 is because they were, in essence, running to extend Joe Biden’s presidency, even after Kamala Harris took over the race. There’s a deep feeling of dissatisfaction in this country. People want change. One of the biggest mistakes Democrats could make is basing their campaigns on going back to “normal.” People don’t want to vote for the same Democrats who seem to be in the process of losing our democracy to Trumpism. To win, Democrats must trumpet a bold, new agenda. For example, there’s an illegal war going on. Oppose it. 2\. Don’t waste time trying to crack the cult. Getting apathetic non-voters to show up at the polls is a more achievable goal. 3\. Don’t focus only on Trump. When Trump is your sole target, you do a favor to every other Republican who enables his fascism. Trump’s not actually on the ballot, and his political lackeys who are running this year will try to create distance from him before the midterms. We want people to vote against Republicans as a group. A good term to use is “Trump Republicans.” 4\. Be a good ally. One of the most exasperating behaviors of progressives is to attack people who agree with them almost all of the time instead of people who always disagree with them. Peter, this month we recognize World Environment Day, World Trails Day, _and_ World Oceans Day, and I can't help but to think about the kind of world we're leaving behind for our children and grandchildren.

As a mom and a pediatrician, I believe every child deserves clean air to breathe, clean water to drink, and healthy communities where they can grow up and thrive.

I want future generations to enjoy the same forests, parks, rivers, and public lands that make Washington such a special place to call home. But the Trump administration doesn't seem to share the same sentiment.

Instead of protecting our planet and safeguarding the natural world, Trump sees public lands as places for industry to mine, drill, and graze. Frankly, his administration has devoted itself to gutting critical environmental protections, weakening safeguards that keep our communities healthy, and making it significantly easier for polluters to damage our public lands.

This administration has put powerful special interests ahead of the people who have to live with the consequences. I simply refuse to sit on the sidelines while that happens.

In Congress, I've fought to protect our natural resources, support conservation efforts, strengthen forest health, and help communities prepare for the growing threat of catastrophic wildfires. clean_body: Peter, this month we recognize World Environment Day, World Trails Day, and World Oceans Day, and I can't help but to think about the kind of world we're leaving behind for our children and grandchildren. As a mom and a pediatrician, I believe every child deserves clean air to breathe, clean water to drink, and healthy communities where they can grow up and thrive. I want future generations to enjoy the same forests, parks, rivers, and public lands that make Washington such a special place to call home. But the Trump administration doesn't seem to share the same sentiment. Instead of protecting our planet and safeguarding the natural world, Trump sees public lands as places for industry to mine, drill, and graze. Frankly, his administration has devoted itself to gutting critical environmental protections, weakening safeguards that keep our communities healthy, and making it significantly easier for polluters to damage our public lands. This administration has put powerful special interests ahead of the people who have to live with the consequences. I simply refuse to sit on the sidelines while that happens. In Congress, I've fought to protect our natural resources, support conservation efforts, strengthen forest health, and help communities prepare for the growing threat of catastrophic wildfires. I've stood up against efforts to roll back protections for our air, water, and public lands because I believe we have a responsibility to leave our communities better than we found them. I'm going to keep fighting back against this administration's attacks on the land we love, and continue to work to protect it. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | = | | = | | = ---|---|---|---|--- = | | = | | = ---|---|---|---|--- Thanks for your continued support. body:
A storm is coming

| | | | | | Peter,
Jen Kiggans' opponent just announced a **staggering $1.75 million raised last quarter.** This is a five-alarm fire, and it's a direct attack on our conservative values. We absolutely cannot afford to lose this fight.
This immense funding poses more than just a threat to Jen's race; it directly threatens our values, our way of life, and the future we want for our children and grandchildren. If the Democrats take Jen's seat, everything that President Trump and our Republican majority have fought to achieve could be undone. If we look the other way on this, things are going to get really bad, really fast: losing President Trump. How? The answer is simple: impeachment.
We both understand what it means to put everything on the line for our country. Having worked with Congresswoman Jen Kiggans before, I can assure you that she is a true patriot and a powerful, steadfast defender of our freedoms. exclusive event. Chris Brooks
Vice President, Membership
League of Conservation Voters Peter, This year on Global Wind Day, you’re personally invited to join LCV, Sierra
Club, and NWF for a special Global Wind Day livestream to celebrate the progress
we’ve made building offshore wind — despite the serious headwinds. You’re Invited: Global Wind Day Livestream

Wednesday, June 10
7 PM ET

name: The Moving Picture Institute
subject: They're Not Teaching Our Kids the Truth
body:
A Patriotic Movie for the 250th
Son of 1776 needs your support to reach millions of young Americans with the true story of America's founding.
[ ](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=2cd8699bcfba4af0a97f327d748be2c8&_e=qo4-GI5BiKC8d3_J56vgCTxVz5_kr7yMWHk_SktSTTnpbCyDTNM5zIJ8dLJ9yN9XOUKvhs2esTRuQqYxAJGqmBfzOC1mkYBN7KOs108ffs8KUHWcpZX-m0WQjyM5_Z0JFI2gy6F1eBXSxM5SZUW8gQo2ORAzMs1_5FwGRD3thSj1rQPXUpA9GdE_j5HkbL5VwXJLU9QDWkQGK_wpgIH_HE5hYoEt7vC72E9X1YGQkyuRer9zkwwxKQ3jPze8TeBnLs-5bdGsaQ9QHm6HxONKnZhx6pYS04Zi20W9YbFWO0N9uhrLYZIzRBwolJRDQulVOLFLlrqtFPIJKgNjT0BJen9QQ7rpIBvgKVu7c7mVGqs58muEJY47wcn2GX7lxH8F2GTNDjuk2drmT5INxJmInbXpOEAxaq7eRyeSttcbKBKFZus5brEwjpmP14sJkoe1VvQ3kabO5EYF-SqZEDvU7P0sSukqF6EuO7awPkNxIuTE2tGVi4bmn2H8XyOtOCevnyQpPQTyxEORZIj_u7kA5cwGRx-c40yjrbi7su4Dm6XwRgyIudxajC_jf_J5yRI1E9ecZGO6RRSb55KSumpBqBQt1e3sHcs5fkMBa6nX8R1__kfKIQ_1CksGBvMnktiBAYjNYi8eLR9EjiDWFtp99h7zCIyom0wuqQ8tInWtWvc%3D)
Hi there,
The way we teach history shapes how the next generation sees America—and right now, that story is changing.
This past Wednesday, I took a closer look at how American history is presented in classrooms today. And what I found was striking. According to a Northwestern University Institute for Policy Research survey, 73% of Americans are dissatisfied with the way the subject is taught in public schools.
That stat tells you everything—parents across the political spectrum recognize that something is wrong.
As you know, these new curricula emphasize systemic challenges and injustices. **Students graduate without understanding the full story—the courage, sacrifice, and vision that built this nation. That's one reason the work of the Moving Picture Institute (MPI) matters so much to me. At MPI, we make movies that highlight the ideals of freedom, character, and service, and help bring these important stories to life for new audiences.**
And this matters more now than ever before. A generation is growing up without access to the stories and films that you and I had. We grew up with movies like _D-Day_ , _Davy Crocket_ , _The Alamo_ , _Top Gun_ —heck, just 20 years ago they made _The Patriot_.
But MPI is counteracting that by making a movie for families with children.

clean_body: A Patriotic Movie for the 250th Son of 1776 needs your support to reach millions of young Americans with the true story of America's founding. Hi there, The way we teach history shapes how the next generation sees America—and right now, that story is changing. This past Wednesday, I took a closer look at how American history is presented in classrooms today. And what I found was striking. According to a Northwestern University Institute for Policy Research survey, 73% of Americans are dissatisfied with the way the subject is taught in public schools. That stat tells you everything—parents across the political spectrum recognize that something is wrong. As you know, these new curricula emphasize systemic challenges and injustices. Students graduate without understanding the full story—the courage, sacrifice, and vision that built this nation. That's one reason the work of the Moving Picture Institute (MPI) matters so much to me. At MPI, we make movies that highlight the ideals of freedom, character, and service, and help bring these important stories to life for new audiences. And this matters more now than ever before. A generation is growing up without access to the stories and films that you and I had. We grew up with movies like D-Day , Davy Crocket , The Alamo , Top Gun —heck, just 20 years ago they made The Patriot. But MPI is counteracting that by making a movie for families with children. Son of 1776 is an animated film where a young patriot joins George Washington and experiences the American Revolution. Children and families will see the bravery and sacrifice that forged this great nation. This is a movie that WILL celebrate America's 250th birthday. | | ---|---|--- | | Sincerely, Joseph Corey Vice President of Philanthropic Investments The Moving Picture Institute | 375 Greenwich Street New York NY 10013

body:
https://alexkelloff.com/ [https://alexkelloff.com/]
A Letter from Alex
This morning I am writing to you from Trinidad, Colorado. That feels appropriate because this is where my great-grandfather and his three brothers immigrated in 1893. As many of you have heard me say, my family's roots in this district go back more than 130 years. Because of those western and southern Colorado roots, I care deeply about what happens here in Colorado's 3rd District.
My primary election on June 30 is exactly three weeks from today. I have been campaigning for more than 13 months and got into this race early because I knew someone needed to hold Donald Trump and Jeff Hurd accountable. Government corruption is rampant, Congress is failing to do its job as a co-equal branch of government, the cost of living is out of control, our public lands and water are at risk, and the American Dream is slipping further out of reach. I have been traveling every corner of this district fighting to change that. And now, the campaign enters its final stretch.
Primary ballots were mailed yesterday, June 8, and should begin arriving in mailboxes across the district in the coming days. If you are planning to vote by mail, do not wait. Ballots must be received by 7:00 p.m. on June 30 to be counted, and election officials recommend mailing them back by June 20. Every vote truly matters. If you have questions about voting, you can find more information at https://justvotecolorado.org/ [https://justvotecolorado.org/]
I rarely ask for anything from you – ok, ok I occasionally ask for financial support 😊 But today, I am asking for something even more important: your vote.
If you are registered as a Democrat or Unaffiliated voter in Colorado's 3rd District, you can vote for me in this primary. And please remind your friends, neighbors, family members, coworkers, and fellow community members to vote. Share our campaign with people who are ready for a representative who will show up, listen, and fight for western and southern Colorado.
It is time to finish what we started. Together, let's win this primary, take back this seat in November, and protect the things that make Colorado's 3rd District so special.
— Alex
May Recap
As the month continued, the momentum behind the "By the People" tour only grew stronger.
Alex visited Glenwood Springs, Meeker, and Paonia, where community members came together to share their perspectives on the issues facing Western Colorado. These conversations continue to reinforce what we hear throughout the district: people want leaders who will listen, show up, and work toward practical solutions on affordability, healthcare, public lands, water, and economic opportunity.
The campaign also saw strong support from communities across the district through several well-attended events. On May 28th, supporters gathered at the home of Alexa Wesner for a successful fundraiser and opportunity to discuss the future of Colorado's 3rd District. We are grateful to Alexa and everyone who attended for their support and engagement.
On May 30th, Alex traveled to Pueblo for a full day of events. Each event brought together community members from across the region and provided another opportunity to hear directly from voters about the challenges and opportunities facing Southern Colorado.
Alex also participated in an event hosted by the Gunnison County Democrats in Marble, where CD-3 candidates, including Alex, created another valuable forum for public conversation and community engagement. Events like these are an important part of ensuring voters have the opportunity to engage directly with candidates and ask questions about the issues that matter most to them.
And while the campaign trail rarely slows down, we took a moment this week to celebrate Alex's birthday. We are grateful for his tireless commitment to traveling the district, listening to communities, and putting in the work every day to earn the trust of voters across Colorado's 3rd District. We hope you'll join us in wishing him a happy birthday as he continues this journey.
Yesterday, the "By the People" tour made a stop in Trinidad, where residents shared their concerns about the direction of the current administration and the challenges they see facing their communities. As with every stop on the tour, Alex's priority was to listen, learn, and ensure that those voices help shape the campaign's vision and the work he hopes to do in Washington.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP62/1/118157/images/Screenshot%202026-06-09%20at%201.17.56%E2%80%AFPM.jpg]
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP62/1/118157/images/Screenshot%202026-06-09%20at%201.18.12%E2%80%AFPM.jpg]
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP62/1/118157/images/Screenshot%202026-06-09%20at%201.18.22%E2%80%AFPM.jpg]
As we head into June, the final stops of the current "By the People" tour will take Alex to Pueblo, Alamosa, Gunnison, and Grand Junction. These visits will continue to shape the campaign's priorities as we work to build a movement grounded in listening, accountability, and community engagement.
Every stop along the way reinforces why this campaign exists: to ensure that the voices of the people of Colorado's 3rd District are heard and represented. We remain committed to meeting people where they are, listening to their concerns, and building a campaign By the People and for the people.
Holding Hurd Accountable
Panicked Ads, Dark Money, and Endless War: Jeff Hurd is flooding local television airwaves with defensive new campaign ads that desperately try to hitch his wagon to Donald Trump. This massive spending blitz is largely coming from outside dark money groups pouring cash into the race to save him from his primary. It is a panicked reaction to a far-right primary opponent who is capitalizing on Hurd's unwillingness to show up in the district, proving that Hurd is terrified of losing his seat and is scrambling for political cover. But while he uses these commercials to kiss the ring of party leadership, his voting record shows he is perfectly comfortable writing blank checks for foreign conflicts.
On June 4, 2026, Hurd voted against a bipartisan war powers resolution that aimed to rein in unauthorized military actions. This decision to prolong a costly war of choice comes at a massive expense to everyday Americans and his own constituents. The resulting international volatility has driven local gas prices to a four-year high and kept inflation climbing across the district. Instead of protecting the economic survival of working families who are struggling to pay for groceries and fuel, Hurd is prioritizing saving his own skin.
What's Coming Soon
We will continue with our By the People tour and have a few more stops. We are looking forward to visiting the various communities across the district and engaging in conversations with you all. Hope to see you there!
* June 9th — Pueblo from 12-1:30pm at Milberger Farms
* June 9th — Alamosa from 5-7pm at The Barn at Manzanilla Farm
* June 11th — Gunnison from 5:30-7pm at Gunnison Library
* June 14th — Grand Junction from 10am-12pm at Mesa County Democrats Office
Where We've Been
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP62/1/118157/images/Screenshot%202026-06-09%20at%201.18.34%E2%80%AFPM.jpg]
You'll also be hearing Alex's voice on the airwaves. Throughout May, Alex joined several podcasts and radio shows to talk about the race and the issues that matter most to Southern and Western Colorado. Alex was on the American Small Business [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8-60N1HICIU] podcast, the The Durango Herald [https://www.durangoherald.com/articles/alex-kelloff-says-cd3-needs-stronger-rural-representation/] , Our Democracy Collective [https://sandiault.substack.com/p/dedicated-to-the-people-sandi-ault] podcast, on Telluride Radio [https://www.kdnk.org/podcast/kdnk-daily-news/2026-05-12/tuesday-may-12] , in The Aspen Times [https://www.aspentimes.com/news/beyond-the-algorithm-keeping-the-lights-on/] , and the Vail Daily [https://www.vaildaily.com/news/in-eagle-countys-other-congressional-district-blue-dog-salazar-explains-the-rural-mindset/] .
If you'd like to add a By the People stop and meet with Alex, ask questions, and share your thoughts, please email campaign@alexkelloff.com [campaign@alexkelloff.com] and a member of our team will follow up quickly to discuss scheduling. We'd also be happy to schedule a virtual meet and greet.
We'd love to hear from you — it's incredibly important that Alex hears from the people he hopes to represent.

3. FINANCIALLY SUPPORT: Donate to my campaign today » [https://secure.numero.ai/contribute/Alex-Kelloff-for-Colorado-web]

4. HOST A MEET & GREET: Contact campaign@alexkelloff.com [campaign@alexkelloff.com] , and we'll quickly follow up with you to discuss hosting an event.

Karp says the AI boys dismissed him - "we're likable, we create value." Delusional idiots.
These tech geniuses are displacing white-collar workers while cozying up to the military only half-heartedly. Politicians smell the massive wealth and want their cut of humanity's collective knowledge. Regulation first, then outright seizure.
Winners? Defense-tied AI plays like Palantir that get government contracts. Karp is positioning smart. Losers? The naive Silicon Valley crowd who think they can keep all the gold without sharing. Next? Pressure builds for AI sovereign wealth funds or forced stakes. Companies that align with national security win big. The rest get regulated to death or nationalized. This is why you build moats with government, not against it. Karp gets it. Most don't.

# **[Korean leveraged ETF's explode in both directions proving these products are retail death traps](https://substack.com/redirect/eb760a2a-d6df-4a5b-aebf-a32ea748b8bb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
**[A Korean leveraged ETF tied to SK Hynix just went completely haywire](https://substack.com/redirect/717cc774-00c6-4309-b053-07f4fcd20b1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** \- plunging 40% while the stock surged 8%, after jumping 50% when the stock tanked. Twice in two days. Market making liquidity dried up at close, spreads blew out, and retail got absolutely torched executing at market prices. These single-stock leveraged products are volatility accelerators on steroids.
South Korea's market is already a casino with Kospi swinging 8% days like it's nothing. New leveraged ETFs on chipmakers launched recently - daily rebalancing forces buying into strength and selling weakness, amplifying every move. Perfect recipe for disaster when liquidity evaporates.
What it really means: leveraged products in volatile names are not for the faint-hearted or the retail crowd. They promise double the daily return but deliver financial carnage when things break. Winners? The house and sharp institutions who understand the mechanics. Losers? Retail punters chasing the AI hype into these things. Next? More scrutiny, possible regulatory heat, and continued wild swings in Korean semis. Stay the hell away unless you're trading this insanity professionally. This is why I say, know your instrument or get destroyed.

Dear Friends,
Last week, something important happened in Salem.
Republicans from every corner of Oregon — candidates, elected officials, county party leaders, and grassroots activists — came together for our GOP Unity Luncheon. The primary season is behind us. The general election is ahead. And the message from every person in that room was the same: we are united.
A defining moment came when gubernatorial nominee Christine Drazan publicly thanked each of the candidates who challenged her in the primary — Chris Dudley, Ed Diehl, David Medina, and Danielle Bethell. One by one, each of them pledged their support and called on their own supporters to unite behind the Republican ticket heading into November.
That kind of unity doesn't happen by accident. It happens because Republicans across Oregon understand what's at stake — for families struggling with the cost of living, for small businesses crushed by red tape, for communities that deserve leadership that actually listens.
As House Republican Leader Lucetta Elmer said: _"This election is bigger than any one of us."_
She's right. And that's why your support right now matters so much. The work of building toward November — candidate support, voter outreach, county party organizing — takes resources. If you believe Oregon deserves a real change in direction, I hope you'll consider joining us in that effort today.
Thank you for everything you do for Oregon.
God bless,
**Connie Whelchel**

clean_body: | | | | Oregon Republicans came together last week. Here's what it means for November. Dear Friends, Last week, something important happened in Salem. Republicans from every corner of Oregon — candidates, elected officials, county party leaders, and grassroots activists — came together for our GOP Unity Luncheon. The primary season is behind us. The general election is ahead. And the message from every person in that room was the same: we are united. A defining moment came when gubernatorial nominee Christine Drazan publicly thanked each of the candidates who challenged her in the primary — Chris Dudley, Ed Diehl, David Medina, and Danielle Bethell. One by one, each of them pledged their support and called on their own supporters to unite behind the Republican ticket heading into November. That kind of unity doesn't happen by accident. It happens because Republicans across Oregon understand what's at stake — for families struggling with the cost of living, for small businesses crushed by red tape, for communities that deserve leadership that actually listens. As House Republican Leader Lucetta Elmer said: "This election is bigger than any one of us." She's right. And that's why your support right now matters so much. The work of building toward November — candidate support, voter outreach, county party organizing — takes resources. From NFL to Congress
This is the game that matters most. I am honored to be in it -- and I would be humbled to have you as my teammate in this fight.

| | | |
---
| | | Hi Peter, My name is Jay Feely. I'm a husband, a father of four, a retired NFL player, sports broadcaster, and a proud Arizona conservative -- **and I'm running for Congress in Arizona's 1st District.** I'll tell you more about my story in a moment. But first, I need you to understand what's at stake in this race -- because it goes far beyond Arizona. **AZ-1 is one of the most targeted House seats in the country in 2026.** Democrats and their allied super PACs already have this race circled. If they flip this seat, they have a path to reclaiming the House majority -- and reversing everything we've fought to build. That is why President Trump and Republican House Leadership have endorsed me in this race, [_**and why I'm writing to you today asking for your support.**_](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=155494b18eda424b8fd2dc7d8045c3a0&_e=--GH1rz24QrFT95w8ydRKXYaIPVl38HQ8MygMDdsfQFvV6AfKLp1JZ_RKk1F_mOBfNRpHWj3kAs1KBllVhUgdkbTAGUb59mL8FIxVFCOI-d0R5jNx08S8xVfnVTYYXBYAJY34uLyXw7ZNYON_sVz6rIz42bpflReNExWUh6jEckjxlX04lz8W7h0O24IL-XxFbpt6JAjwVCHm32puPbpdwpAMlhDyo4IwjiNNtXxMaQPfYixbvqZ_Ji4mnz5OreszuuOZUY8sRbIuotaJf3te60dhVXXvvnJ4rB9GCeWRPb5hT3SRcYp1Ava-rKenEAKmNJ9y76MBr3VyuPpRmJXPXU1-omPVi1ogJk0w4pjlctHq1KHQPhi-U0dTESz-L2EMK8jHh5xuExdEIMfCqaRVFmefbpoGy1unZZp66IuJ_DTNDHKetJpLgSSoEai6K65_se3oN_Ko--ZU4Vy1LfWo6U1vsmTNBbnC5j_i9GNbasuqZolU-XuPzJLAkz4NnklDz02leldWyQpIVzxhSRmiobdJeLONuxyXr4-Lb01fTgArolo7-pHJpuxi475782V23SFdvNdHIRbeGcfCZC25i8kQq5PayfQDqHjUWRGTg9oYKUTLDdtK0V0KFAqE6u0LbgJ4hVIb6eVSEPjI2yJShlsZ9n6vJO-DzlNXF9l49Whh-cLqmj2-VF6I0ChjVU6WHemLAtD59GxjOp7qlVcNg%3D%3D)

Now -- let me tell you who I am and why I believe God has called me to this fight.I grew up in a middle-class family in Florida, and was taught from a young age that **our blessings aren't meant to be hoarded -- they're meant to be poured out for others.** That truth has shaped every chapter of my life. I earned a scholarship to the University of Michigan, won a National Championship in 1997, and went on to play fourteen years in the NFL.I wasn't the biggest or the fastest player on the field. But I was elected team captain on three different teams because my teammates trusted me to lead with integrity and fight for what was right.

When the NFL went into lockout negotiations, my fellow players sent me to Washington to sit across the table from ownership at the Federal mediation office. **I didn't back down then. I won't back down in Congress either.** After football, I spent ten years as an NFL analyst for CBS, earning five Emmy Awards along the way. But the work I'm most proud of has nothing to do with broadcast booths or trophies.My wife Rebecca and I fell in love with Arizona fifteen years ago when I signed with the Cardinals. We loved it so much we decided it was the perfect place to raise our family -- and we've been putting down roots here ever since. We founded the Feely Family Foundation to invest in youth and education. I served on the Gilbert Christian School Board. I started the first girls' soccer program at Gilbert Christian High School, coached our daughter Lexi's team to a state championship, and was named Arizona State Coach of the Year.

**_The border crisis is real_** , and it has impacted communities like ours every single day -- straining our schools, our hospitals, our law enforcement, and our neighborhoods.Our **_small business owners_** are being crushed by taxes and federal regulations that punish hard work and reward dependency. Friend,
The primary race is coming to an end on June 30, and we need to be honest with you—we are being outspent at a moment when everything matters.
David’s opponents see him as a threat to the status quo, which enables the wealthy to get more powerful while working families suffer. They have more money, more resources, and more institutional support, but what we have is something stronger: people like you.
Right now, we’re out in the field doing the work that actually wins elections. And we need to fund paying for clipboards, printing literature, and supporting volunteers who are knocking on doors and talking to voters face to face. That work doesn’t happen without resources behind it.
If you’re able, can you chip in today to help us stay competitive in this final stretch? We have a reporting deadline tomorrow, and every dollar right now goes directly to keeping this field program alive and growing. Friend,

Whether I’m knocking on doors, meeting with volunteers, or catching up with folks at events like our Women in Leadership Brunch this past weekend, I keep getting asked the exact same question:

"Sarah, where can my resources make the absolute biggest impact to win back the House?"

My answer is always: Janelle Stelson.

I was so incredibly proud to host Janelle in Annapolis over the weekend. She is running as an official DCCC Red to Blue candidate for Congress up in Pennsylvania's 10th district, and let me tell you, she is exactly the kind of independent, pragmatic leader we need in Washington.

If we want to build a forward-looking majority that can actually protect fundamental rights and deliver practical results for families, Democrats have to win in Districts just like hers. I believe Janelle’s race is our best opportunity to flip a seat this cycle. But the truth is: beating the former Chair of the Freedom Caucus requires resources and grassroots organizing.

That’s why Janelle and I are teaming up. In July, we will be bringing our summer fellows and Do-Something Democrat volunteers to Pennsylvania to knock on hundreds of doors for Janelle.

Together, we’ve already raised thousands of dollars on Janelle’s behalf — but we are not quite at our goal. Every single dollar raised from this email will be split evenly between our campaigns so we can keep our organizers hitting the pavement through June.

body:
Trump wants to place gag orders on federal employees to keep his illegal activity in the dark. It’s a move he stole right out of the Supreme Court’s playbook. | |
---
Peter, Whistleblowers are vital to our democracy. They make sure the public is informed about how our government is working, and whether we need to speak out against shady, illegal activity. **Trump is trying to change all that. He wants to make sure every federal employee is loyal to him, not the people—and that if they speak out, they get punished.** The Trump administration just announced a plan to roll out nondisclosure agreements across the federal government. He wants to keep federal workers from speaking to the media about the wrongdoing they witness. **Like when a DOGE employee stole the Social Security file containing everyone’s personal information.** **Where did they get the idea from? You guessed it, the captured Roberts Supreme Court.** In 2024, they put gag orders on all Supreme Court employees to keep them from telling the public about what they were seeing at the Court. We the People deserve to know about the abuses, wrongdoing, and illegal activity federal employees witness. And federal workers deserve their First Amendment right to speak out. **[The Office of Personnel Management is accepting official comments on Trump’s plan to silence federal workers. Add your name to an official comment using this simple form now!](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3_ENTPUFXS71HakIlAJZ9Hr3UVVc_dMjtZNELLPGnK2daHQjxIDWCLwlgg1HZ9UfgYAxz_M3-zkXQAMlujYGgrAD_ynqp4CZK9AQ2qvnWqtJeNyzqJ37oRjrACHAL1g_lJ3r-ht0aDfQdISf3P_6ZxDzTTchI1OYZ7ItL7bOW4Is7Mb9OSXAwxjSleaYbuBlDlkrc87pvVEiW5aDu89oEZIGw2llPePycMcwq-soC8WV5g3ASBiGWwWlZhk_jf6_x44lU7HUoGYLJEJOro4MddcAB8c7o94Go_8nA5kkzBkTp_P7SOcBbn8KUSSd8_wOHVzF2hYhNhUlEheR13cbS2B8bRFTeOgHuaSFoV4g8rDG1Jhv0BBkRrYLPKKlvXrMKJUN0utwlGQz-jQ7DEpLo4Us6LtFS1XKwmV0sTZeuWN-lfH7OonQUVPDb6oDdQIDN7RJi6b1U3w_fH9uf7KOSC6/4rc/whYe1WYWQAqK_VvokSyLDA/h0/h001.H3QUnCHjMQpoK-1Ms2uRogUoRzoXL_w7H_iz2mUcaDs)** **** [ADD YOUR NAME](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3_ENTPUFXS71HakIlAJZ9Hr3UVVc_dMjtZNELLPGnK2daHQjxIDWCLwlgg1HZ9UfgYAxz_M3-zkXQAMlujYGgrAD_ynqp4CZK9AQ2qvnWqtJeNyzqJ37oRjrACHAL1g_lJ3r-ht0aDfQdISf3P_6ZxDzTTchI1OYZ7ItL7bOW4Is7Mb9OSXAwxjSleaYbuBlDlkrc87pvVEiW5aDu89oEZIGw2llPePycMcwq-soC8WV5g3ASBiGWwWlZhk_jf6_x5f_lYaU3dpn99cBKYZV_DkszyVkdFZ3Gc0HHDADuiTzjyKf9HfBjyIPjmaoYypnr8vZZJNxzWBkOrQNT3YshlM0Fs0zvkFiOFTyQZ3FCqRtlYHx2vNOxxe9orXkxd1Cb_B96eieGF4Xnv25vd59HzovR_M4wUkAlmDsrdZdnQePtMOHJMqrCWm1NbtsdjCaRaHiFH7B42UUxOq4ps8ZTDm/4rc/whYe1WYWQAqK_VvokSyLDA/h1/h001.gQRbbgc8Jz_CD3CoOkRBrQpM-ABeQixNJoJT7DYO0Jg) **Lawyers have warned that the Trump administration gag orders could violate the First Amendment rights of federal employees.** A government employee’s speech is protected when they speak out as a private citizen. # PLYMOUTH NH FUNDRAISER ON JUNE 10TH
and
GRAHAM PLATNER QUESTION

**PLYMOUTH NH FUNDRAISER ON JUNE 10TH**

Please join us on June 10th Wednesday, stop by anytime between 3pm and 6pm at the Common Man Inn. Refreshment will be provided.

Lily’s campaign is built from the ground up by regular, hard-working people who are tired of cost of living increase crushing their household budgets, unchecked government overreach, and the erosion of their liberty.

[Signup for Common Man Event Here](https://us.list-manage.com/q6F3C05lCIv?e=c338950e03&c2id=adf8b61e01be85c238f26a96cfd7c41c)
Wednesday, June 10 at 3:00 – 6:00 pm Eastern Time
The Common Man Inn Plymouth
231 Main St.
Plymouth, NH

**GOODLANDER SILENCE ON GRAHAM PLATNER**

Here is the gist of my Press Release put out this morning:

Republican congressional candidate Lily Tang Williams today called on Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander to answer a simple question: Does she support Maine Democrat U.S. Senate candidate Graham Platner in light of the constant national news coverage and growing controversy surrounding his campaign?

This top-tier Senate race is happening just over our border. The latest allegations that Platner was physically abusive to his partners are very serious and disturbing. As national and state Democrats continue to rally around Platner's Senate bid, voters deserve to know whether Goodlander, as a woman herself, stands with him and supports his candidacy. Additionally, will Maggie Goodlander condemn organizations that support her, like VoteVets, for also propping up Graham Platner?

"Granite Staters always deserve transparency and honesty from their elected officials," said Williams. "Graham Platner is looking to join Maggie as part of the New England delegation in Congress. Maggie Goodlander should tell voters whether she stands with Graham Platner and whether she believes he is fit to represent Maine in the United States Senate."

"If Maggie Goodlander is willing to campaign alongside Graham Platner, raise money for him, or endorse him, the people of New Hampshire have a right to know," Williams continued. "If she believes his conduct or actions are disqualifying, she should say that too. Remaining silent is not leadership."
Lily Tang Williams emphasized that accountability should apply equally to politicians of both parties. "Public officials should be held to the same standards regardless of party affiliation," said Williams. "Independent-minded Granite State voters expect their leaders to speak clearly and honestly when questions arise about the character and conduct of candidates seeking higher office."

Williams called on Rep. Goodlander to publicly state whether she supports Platner's candidacy and whether she intends to endorse, campaign for, or assist his Senate campaign.

[Donate Here](https://us.list-manage.com/pmcphjhDdPG?e=c338950e03&c2id=adf8b61e01be85c238f26a96cfd7c41c)

Always yours,

Lily Tang Williams
Republican Congressional Candidate NH-2

"Public officials should be held to the same standards regardless of party affiliation," said Williams. "Independent-minded Granite State voters expect their leaders to speak clearly and honestly when questions arise about the character and conduct of candidates seeking higher office." Williams called on Rep. Goodlander to publicly state whether she supports Platner's candidacy and whether she intends to endorse, campaign for, or assist his Senate campaign. body:
What happened in NYC wasn’t a NYC story. This movement is just getting started.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260609-1&t=1&akid=3579%2E587540%2EG4Gafm)
Peter,
I took the oath of office just after midnight on New Year’s Day, in a historic decommissioned subway station beneath City Hall.
No fanfare, just the hum of the city above us, and the feeling that something had shifted.
An energy that had been building for months in living rooms and community centers, on doorsteps and street corners, and in the hearts of people who had been told for too long that the system wasn’t for them.
**For the first time in a long time, it felt like it was.**
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260609_1_mamdani.lXswnu&refcode=em20260609-3579&t=2&akid=3579%2E587540%2EG4Gafm)
When I first announced my campaign for mayor, I was polling at 1%. I was a state assemblyman from Queens running against one of the most powerful political machines in the country. The establishment wrote us off before we even got started.
But they forgot to account for something: the extraordinary coalition of working people, immigrants, young people, and first-time voters who decided that this city could be different.
**3 out of 4 voters under 30 voted for our campaign. Youth turnout was among the highest ever recorded for a municipal election in this country.**
Young people didn’t just cast ballots. They knocked doors, organized their neighbors, and built a compelling movement that mobilized a city. _They made our victory possible._ And Leaders We Deserve played a crucial role in that work.
**I’d like to take a moment to tell you about the first time I met Leaders We Deserve’s cofounder, David Hogg.**
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260609_1_mamdani.lXswnu&refcode=em20260609-3579&t=3&akid=3579%2E587540%2EG4Gafm)
My race was one of Leaders’ first endorsements of 2025, and in the lead up to the primary election, David came to New York to help me get out the vote. We wanted to film a video together encouraging people to vote early, so we decided to meet in Washington Square Park. It quickly became clear that filming a 30 second video together in the middle of a park would be easier said than done. But what ended up happening was far better than we could have planned. With every attempted take, we were quickly approached by another young person excited to talk to us about their political views, their thoughts on my platform, their excitement about the next generation of leaders, and our shared determination to turn the page on the politics of the past.
Those few hours in Washington Square Park told a story about what becomes possible when a generation decides it’s done waiting. When young people stop being told their issues are too radical, their candidates are unelectable, and their vision is unrealistic. And then work to prove the entire establishment wrong.
That record-breaking coalition of young people didn’t just elect a mayor. It proved something that I believe with everything I am: When people are offered a real vision, not just opposition to the other side, but actual solutions to the cost of living, housing, health care, and the systems that have failed working families for too long — they _will_ show up.
**But here’s what I need you to understand: what happened in New York City was not just a New York City story.**
The problems we’re taking on in New York — rent that’s too high, health care out of reach, and a political class more loyal to donors than the people they represent — **those are the same problems working families are dealing with in every corner of this country.**
And there are real solutions to these issues, but we need courageous leaders who are ready to step up and fight for them.
**That’s why Leaders We Deserve’s work is so important. As I said, my race was one of their first endorsements of 2025, and because of supporters like you they’ve spent every day since finding even more next generation fighters to help propel to victory.** People like my friend Claire Valdez, who is running for Congress in NY-07 with the same fearlessness and working class conviction that powered our campaign. And Demi Palecek who recently won her primary in Illinois against the corporate PACs and dark money that tried to buy her seat.
These are our people. This is our moment. And this movement does not stop at the five boroughs.
**[So, will you pitch in $5 today to help my friends at Leaders We Deserve continue backing bold, forward-thinking progressives who will fight for you with urgency and courage?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260609_1_mamdani.lXswnu&refcode=em20260609-3579&amount=5&t=4&akid=3579%2E587540%2EG4Gafm)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260609_1_mamdani.lXswnu&amount=5&refcode=em20260609-3579&t=23&akid=3579%2E587540%2EG4Gafm)**
Thank you for your support. Our wins wouldn’t be possible without you, Peter. Onward.
With solidarity,
Mayor Zohran Mamdani

Let’s build a better Wisconsin for our kids
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260609-2900)
Peter,
Ten years ago today, my life changed forever. And the world got a little brighter.
Happy birthday, George!
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260609.ZSgolm&refcode=em20260609-2900&t=1&akid=2900%2E105371%2ElFhNpA)
It's not easy being a kid these days. It's even harder being a kid whose mom is running a statewide campaign for governor. We’ve gotten used to the long days, dinners cut short by phone calls, strangers who have plenty of opinions about his mom.
The future I want for George is the one I want for every kid in this state — public schools that are fully funded, childcare that families can actually afford, healthcare that doesn’t break the bank. Oh, and freedom from AI data centers.
We’re building a Wisconsin where a good life isn't a privilege for the few but a promise to everyone. That hope is what this campaign runs on.
But time is running out. The primary is just 63 days away, and we have the biggest fundraising deadline of the campaign coming up on June 30,
[So for George's birthday, we’d both be so grateful if you'd mark the day with us and chip in what you can to keep this fight going.](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260609.ZSgolm&refcode=em20260609-2900&t=2&akid=2900%2E105371%2ElFhNpA)

Team,
In 2018, I put my name on a ballot to challenge my State Senator, the Republican incumbent who had won his last race by **16 points**.
When I told some of my local Democratic party leadership that I wanted to challenge him, they said, “Oh honey, that’s _cute_. You don’t have a chance.”
But when all the votes were counted on election night, we beat that guy by **4 points.**
Here’s the lesson:
If anyone ever tells you an area is too red, or not worth fighting for: _That’s bullshit._
We can organize anywhere.
We can flip red seats.
We can even flip entire chambers.
It won’t be easy, but I am more than willing to put in the hard work. Are you with me?

| | Our law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and judges put their lives on the line every single day, and right now, anyone can publish their home address online to threaten them and their families.

Again.** They already hold 75 of 99 seats in the Tennessee House and 27 of 33 in the Senate. **And somehow, that’s not enough.** This week, Senate Republicans signaled that they're considering redrawing the state legislature’s district maps as early as 2027. **Five years before it's supposed to happen.** Right after they just redrew Tennessee's congressional maps mid-election cycle. Tennessee is already one of the most gerrymandered states in the country. For over a decade, Republicans have rigged the rules and manipulated the maps to silence voters and gain one-party control. _**And what do we get?**_ Rising grocery prices, higher gas and hospital bills, lower life expectancy, underfunded public schools, and fewer opportunities for working families. Hi friend,
As ballots continue arriving across Colorado, I've been back out on the road for our By the People Tour.
http://secure.actblue.com/donate/2606-q2-ak? [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/2606-q2-ak?]
Over the last few weeks, I've had the chance to sit down with people in Glenwood Springs, Meeker, and other communities across Western Colorado. And while every town has its own character, one concern keeps coming up.
The economy.
Small business owners are working harder than ever just to keep up with rising costs. Families are feeling squeezed by higher prices. People are worried about what comes next and frustrated that Washington seems more focused on political fights than the challenges they face every day.
Those aren't unreasonable expectations, and it’s why I'm running to represent Colorado's 3rd Congressional District in Congress.
These next two weeks are critical. Will you contribute $25, $50, or whatever you can today to help us fund voter outreach and reach more undecided voters across the district? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/2606-q2-ak?;&]
